A 600 by 600 tile is 3600 cm2, so the calculator starts on double gluing.

pidilite-puma/pegoland-elastic.source: Coverage: 1.5 - 1.9 m2 per 4 kg pack at 1.5 mm bed thickness (using 3 mm x 3 mm notch), 0.74 - 0.93 m2 per 4 kg pack at 3 mm bed thickness (using 6 mm x 6 mm notch). Shown as kg per m2 by dividing 4 kg by the printed area. Rate is for the mixed A plus B product.

tiers.label: 3 mm bed, 6 x 6 mm notch

pidilite-puma/pegoland-elastic.caveat: Two component reaction resin adhesive, class R2T. The figures are for the mixed product. Note the sheet's own inconsistency: the coverage rows are quoted against a 4 kg pack while PACKAGING AND STORAGE gives an 8 Kg two component pail, so one pail is two of the printed units. The sheet also says coverage will vary depending on trowel notch size and type, tile size and how smooth and even the substrate is.

mapei/keraflex-maxi-s1-zero.source: CONSUMPTION: 1.2 kg/m2 per mm of thickness. The sheet also states it can be applied at high thicknesses, up to 15 mm, with no drop.
mapei/keraflex-maxi-s1-zero.caveat: The sheet prints a maximum thickness of 15 mm and no minimum, so the 2 mm floor and the 5 mm default are the calculator's rather than the manufacturer's. This is the thick bed grade of the Keraflex family, which is why the default sits above a normal thin bed. The sheet prints no notched trowel table, so there are no trowel tiers to choose between.

kerakoll/geolite-microsilicato.source: Coverage on fine-texture finished substrate: approx. 0.35 l/m2 for two coats

kerakoll/geolite-microsilicato.caveat: The printed figure is the total for two coats, so it is not multiplied by a coat count. The sheet says the product may be applied in more coats according to the level of coverage and colour effect required.

kerakoll/biocalce-rinzaffo.source: Coverage: approx. 15 kg/m2 per cm of thickness
kerakoll/biocalce-rinzaffo.caveat: The sheet prints the rate per centimetre, 15 kg/m2 per cm, which is 1.5 kg/m2 per mm. Minimum thickness obtainable is about 5 mm and the sheet states no maximum, so the upper bound here is ours, not the sheet's.

kerakoll/biocalce-silicato-fondo.caveat: The technical data table prints 0.15 to 0.25 l/m2 for each coat while the body text prints approx. 0.25 l/m2 per single coat. The wider table range is used here. A second coat is recommended.

kerakoll/biocalce-silicato-fondo-fino.source: Coverage: approx. 0.1 - 0.2 l/m2 per single coat

The sheet prints no second coat rate for porous substrates. It asks for 1 coat as a filler undercoat, 2 as a colour coating and 3 for very bright colours.

The system involves a minimum of 2 coats, and the product may be diluted up to 10% with water.

mapei/mapefloor-fc-200-me.source: CONSUMPTION, multi-layered roll coat or structured finish coating: Primer SN (A+B) 0.15-0.25 kg/m2 if required, 1st coat Mapefloor FC 200 ME (A+B) 0.32 kg/m2, finishing coat Mapefloor FC 200 ME (A+B) 0.32 kg/m2

Mapefloor I 300 SL ME, smooth self-levelling at average 2 mm

mapei/mapefloor-i-300-sl-me.caveat: A layered system, not a single rate. The primer is 0.3 kg/m2 and the body coat is 3.7 kg/m2, so quoting the primer figure as the product rate is twelve times too small. The sheet also says the recommended total consumption of Mapefloor I 300 SL ME must be at least 2.5-3.5 kg/m2, which disagrees with the 3.7 kg/m2 in the consumption list, and a 47 kg unit yields 25.4 litres of mixed material.

mapei/mapefloor-i-300-sl-trp.source: CONSUMPTION: Mapefloor I 300 SL TRP approx. 1.1 kg/m2 to form a 1 mm thick coat

pack.label: kit, component A 12 kg plus component B 6 kg

mapei/mapefloor-i-300-sl-trp.caveat: The product is a top self-levelling layer of approx. 1 mm and the sheet says not to exceed the indicated thickness, so the thickness is fixed at 1 mm rather than open.

It then says consumption will vary significantly with density, porosity, texture, surface absorption, weather, application method and the number of coats, and it does not say how many coats. The drum is sold by weight, 5 kg, and holds 4.8 litres.

mapei/ultracare-acid-cleaner.reason: The sheet prints a CONSUMPTION heading with nothing under it. It says only that consumption varies with dilution, the degree and type of dirt and the surface, so there is no rate to calculate from. The product is supplied in 1 and 5 litre tanks.

mapei/ultracare-epoxy-off-gel.source: CONSUMPTION: with 1 litre of UltraCare Epoxy Off Gel it is possible to clean up to a maximum of 15 m2 of surface

mapei/ultracare-epoxy-off-gel.caveat: The sheet publishes a maximum area per litre, which is inverted here into litres per square metre, so the figure is a best case and consumption may be higher. It varies with the surface and the degree of dirt.

mapei/ultracare-fuga-fresca.reason: The sheet says only that consumption varies depending on the size of the tiles and the grout lines, and publishes no rate for either, so there is nothing to calculate from. The product is supplied in a 1 kg bucket and a 160 g sponge applicator bottle.

mapei/ultracare-grout-release.source: CONSUMPTION: up to 40 m2 of surface with 1 litre of UltraCare Grout Release (one coat)

tiers.hint: Up to 40 m2 per litre inverted, so at least 0.025 litres per m2

mapei/ultracare-grout-release.caveat: The sheet publishes an area per litre for one coat, which is inverted here into litres per square metre. It is a best case: yield is heavily influenced by the absorbency and the surface finish of the substrate.

mapei/ultracare-hd-cleaner.source: CONSUMPTION: one litre diluted 1:20 with water cleans approximately 200 m2; diluted 1:5 with water coverage is approximately 30 m2

tiers.label: Diluted 1:20 with water
tiers.hint: 200 m2 per litre of concentrate inverted

tiers.label: Diluted 1:5 with water
tiers.hint: 30 m2 per litre of concentrate inverted

mapei/ultracare-hd-cleaner.caveat: Both rates are litres of undiluted concentrate per square metre, inverted from the areas per litre the sheet publishes. The stronger 1:5 dilution is the default because it is the higher consuming of the two. Consumption depends on the dilution, the degree and type of dirt and the surface.

mapei/ultracare-intensifier-s.source: CONSUMPTION: up to 30 m2 surface with 1 litre of UltraCare Intensifier S (one coat)

tiers.hint: Up to 30 m2 per litre inverted, so at least 0.033 litres per m2

mapei/ultracare-intensifier-s.caveat: The sheet publishes an area per litre for one coat, which is inverted here into litres per square metre, and it is a best case: yield is strongly influenced by the absorbency and the surface finish. Additional coats may be applied to enhance the colour further, so the coat count is the user's choice and the sheet's own basis is one coat.

mapei/ultracare-intensifier-w.source: CONSUMPTION: up to 30 m2 surface with 1 litre of UltraCare Intensifier W (one coat)

mapei/ultracare-kerapoxy-cleaner.reason: The sheet says only that consumption varies with the degree and type of dirt and the surface to be treated, and publishes no rate, so there is nothing to calculate from. The product is supplied in 750 ml spray bottles and 5 litre tanks.

The tape itself is Ultrabond Turf Tape, which has its own roll calculator.

kerakoll/b3.reason: The sheet quotes coverage by length, not by area: approximately 30 g per metre of tongue and groove joint, from 500 g bottles. mapei/ultracolor-plus.source: The sheet prints the formula itself on its consumption page: (A + B) / (A x B) x C x D x 1,6 = kg/m2, with A and B the tile length and width, C the thickness and D the joint width, all in millimetres. 1.6 reproduces all 130 printed cells of its consumption table.

mapei/keracolor-ff.source: The sheet prints the formula as (A + B) / (A x B) x C x D x 1.5 = kg/m2, to one decimal place. 1.519 is the value within that printed precision which reproduces all 39 printed cells of its consumption table; a flat 1.5 misses one.

mapei/fugolastic.reason: The sheet gives no rate of its own. Fugolastic is a latex additive for Keracolor grouts and its CONSUMPTION line reads: the consumption of Fugolastic depends on the consumption of Keracolor. Size the Keracolor first, then dose the Fugolastic from the Keracolor sheet.

mapei/kerapoxy.source: Fitted to the printed consumption table. 1.6 reproduces all 108 printed cells, and is the constant Mapei prints in plain text on the Kerapoxy CQ sheet for the same formula.

pack.label: pre dosed unit, component A plus component B

mapei/kerapoxy-cq.source: The sheet prints the constant itself: FORMULA FOR THE COVERAGE CALCULATION, (A + B) kg x C x D x 1.6 = (A x B) m2. It reproduces all 108 printed cells.

mapei/kerapoxy-easy-design.source: Kerapoxy Easy Design shares its 108 cell table with Kerapoxy CQ, whose sheet prints the constant 1.6 in plain text. 1.6 reproduces all 108 cells; the 1.55 derived from the density of the mix reproduces 87.

pack.label: pre dosed drum, component A plus component B

mapei/kerapoxy-adhesive.source: CONSUMPTION: consumption is 1.5 kg/m2 per millimetre of thickness.

pack.label: kit, component A 8 kg plus component B 2 kg

mapei/kerapoxy-adhesive.caveat: Filed with the epoxy grouts but this is an adhesive, so it takes a rate per millimetre and not the joint formula. The sheet gives no recommended thickness, only that it is applied at a thickness of up to 1 cm in one single coat, so the 10 mm bound is the sheet's maximum and the 5 mm starting point is not a sheet figure.

mapei/mapefill-gp-me.source: CONSUMPTION: every 25 kg bag of Mapefill GP ME yields 13-14 litres of grout. A 25 kg bag over the lower 13 litre yield is 1.92 kg of powder per litre of grout.
mapei/mapefill-gp-me.caveat: The yield is printed as a range of 13 to 14 litres per bag. The lower yield is used so the bag count does not fall short; at 14 litres the figure is 1.79 kg per litre. The sheet prints no minimum or maximum gap, so the gap range offered is a working range and not a sheet figure.

mapei/mapefill-sp-me.source: CONSUMPTION: every 25 kg bag of Mapefill SP ME yields 13-14 litres of grout. A 25 kg bag over the lower 13 litre yield is 1.92 kg of powder per litre of grout.
mapei/mapefill-sp-me.caveat: The yield is printed as a range of 13 to 14 litres per bag. The lower yield is used so the bag count does not fall short; at 14 litres the figure is 1.79 kg per litre. The sheet says a thickness of 60 mm should not be exceeded for rigid joints, and to consult the manufacturer for cavities greater than 100 mm.

mapei/mapegrout-pt-me.reason: Mapegrout PT ME is an injection grout for filling and repairing post tensioning ducts, so there is no area to calculate: a 25 kg bag yields approximately 16 to 17 litres of grout and the quantity is the volume of the ducts. The sheet says in terms not to use it for precision grouting, and names Mapefill SP ME for that instead.

kerakoll/fugabella-color.source: Coverage table, grammes/m2 by format, thickness and joint width: 60x60 cm at 10 mm thickness and a 3 mm joint prints approx 190 g/m2, which is 0.19 kg/m2. The constant 1.900 is fitted to that table and reproduces all 196 printed cells to the nearest gramme.
kerakoll/fugabella-color.caveat: Also supplied in 3 kg bags. The sheet states that its coverage figures are averaged out based on our experience and taking into account normal site wastage, so no further wastage allowance should be added. The design study fitted 1.897 from a 28 cell sample; across the full 196 cell table the constant is 1.900, which is the figure used here.

kerakoll/fugalite-color.source: Coverage table, grammes/m2 by format, thickness and joint width: 60x60 cm at 10 mm thickness prints approx 55 g/m2 at a 1 mm joint and approx 111 at 2 mm. The constant 1.660 is fitted to that table and reproduces all 68 printed cells to the nearest gramme, and it matches the printed specific weight of the mixture of 1.66 kg/dm3.

pack.label: monopack, part A 3 kg plus part B 1 kg

kerakoll/fugalite-color.caveat: Also supplied as a 1 kg monopack, part A 0.75 kg plus part B 0.25 kg. The table states it already takes normal site wastage into account, so no further allowance should be added. Its joint width columns are 1, 2, 5 and 10 mm, so a 3 mm joint is interpolated by the formula rather than read off a printed column. Used as an adhesive the consumption is approx 2 to 4 kg/m2 and the joint inputs do not apply. Joint width range is 0 to 10 mm.

kerakoll/fugalite-invisibile.source: Coverage table, grammes/m2 by format, thickness and joint width: 60x60 cm at 10 mm thickness and a 3 mm joint prints approx 180 g/m2. The constant 1.820 is fitted to that table and reproduces 34 of the 54 printed cells at the printed step, with 45 of 54 within 3 percent and 51 of 54 within 5 percent.

pack.label: monopack, part A 2.82 kg plus part B 0.18 kg

kerakoll/fugalite-invisibile.caveat: This table is rounded coarsely, to the nearest 5 or 10 grammes, and its own rows imply constants from 1.75 to 1.88, so a single constant cannot reproduce every cell. The worst outlier is 30x60 cm at 4 mm thickness, printed as approx 40 g/m2 where the formula gives 36. The table states it already takes normal site wastage into account, which is why the figure sits well above the printed specific weight of the mixture of 1.55 kg/dm3. Joint width range is 0 to 3 mm. Used as an adhesive the consumption is approx 2 to 4 kg/m2 and the joint inputs do not apply.

kerakoll/fugaflex.reason: The sheet gives a dosage, not a rate per square metre. Fugaflex is a latex additive measured against the bag of grout it goes into: approx 0.35 kg per 3 kg bag or approx 2.25 kg per 20 kg bag of Fugabella Color, and approx 2 kg per 20 kg bag of Fugarok. Size the grout first, then read the dosage off that bag count.

tiers.hint: The sheet prints one coverage range and says the product can be diluted in water in any ratio

kerakoll/delta-plus.caveat: Also supplied in 1 kg cans. This is an acid detergent for cement and lime residues, not a grout, so it is priced per square metre of surface cleaned. Do not use on marble or calcareous stone, and wait at least 7 days on normal setting cement grouts and 3 days on rapid setting ones.

kerakoll/aquastop-bt.source: Technical Data: Roll width 150 mm. Roll length 15 m. Total thickness 0,8 mm. Instructions for use: remove the lower half of the protective silicon film and fix Aquastop BT to the screed along the joint between wall and floor, then fix it to the wall.

Nothing is added here for a lap between successive pieces, because the sheet prints none: that is a bound the sheet does not print, so allow for it on site. The 5 mm gap the sheet asks for between the membrane and the wall is a detail of the membrane above and not a lap in the tape. The waterproofing product that covers it, the Aquastop Fix sealant and the Aquastop 120 tape over the edge are separate products with their own rates.

Measure the metres of perimeter or joint, read 0.6 kg per metre, and order in 6 kg buckets, which is about 10 metres a bucket.

mapei/planiseal-288.caveat: In tanks and swimming pools the sheet asks for at least three coats to form a layer 3 mm thick, which is the third coat here. The sheet forbids more than 2 mm per coat. The consumption figure is for a seamless film on a flat surface and is higher on uneven substrates, which the sheet does not quantify.

mapei/planiseal-88.source: CONSUMPTION: 1.5 kg/m2 per mm of thickness.

tiers.label: Brush, trowel or spray, 1 mm per coat
tiers.hint: The final thickness should be approximately 2 to 3 mm

mapei/planiseal-88.caveat: The sheet asks for a final thickness of approximately 2 to 3 mm and says application by brush may require 2 to 3 coats, so three coats is within spec and two is the minimum. By trowel, the first coat should be brushed on. This is a rigid waterproofing and the sheet says it must not be exposed to vehicular traffic.

pidilite-puma/morcem-dry-sf-plus.reason: The sheet prints the build up but no rate: a second coat after the first has dried, a total thickness including the reinforcing fabric of 2 to 2.5 mm, a minimum of 2 mm, and not more than 2 mm of wet film per layer. There is no kg/m2 or kg/m2 per mm anywhere on it, so any quantity would be invented. Supplied as 25 kg powder plus 10 kg latex. Ask us and we will quote against the thickness.

mapei/mapenet-150.source: PACKAGING: 50 metre rolls, 1 m wide. APPLICATION: overlap each piece of Mapenet 150 by at least 5 cm.
mapei/mapenet-150.caveat: The sheet publishes no consumption rate: Mapenet 150 is an alkali resistant glass fibre mesh bedded into the waterproofing layer rather than spread. The quantity here is the length of mesh the area needs once the 5 cm lap is allowed for. The transverse laps at the end of each roll are not counted, so on a job made of many short runs order one roll over.

mapei/mapegrout-t60-me.caveat: The sheet publishes a yield in litres of mortar per bag rather than a rate, so the rate here is 25 kg divided by 12.6 litres, which is 1.98 kg of powder per litre of mortar, and one square metre at one millimetre is one litre. Applied at a minimum thickness of 10 mm up to 60 mm in a single layer.

kerakoll/active-prime-fix.source: COVERAGE: approximately 0.1 to 0.2 kg/m2, applied with a medium bristle synthetic fibre roller.

tiers.label: Roller coat on the prepared substrate
tiers.hint: One coat before a levelling compound

kerakoll/active-prime-fix.caveat: A primer, so the rate is per square metre and does not depend on thickness. Also supplied in 1 kg bottles and 5 kg buckets.

kerakoll/active-prime-grip.source: COVERAGE: approximately 0.2 to 0.3 kg/m2, applied with a medium bristle synthetic fibre roller.

tiers.label: Roller coat on the prepared substrate
tiers.hint: One coat on non absorbent substrates

kerakoll/active-prime-grip.caveat: A primer, so the rate is per square metre and does not depend on thickness. Also supplied in 5 kg buckets.

kerakoll/geolite.source: COVERAGE: approximately 17 kg/m2 per cm of thickness.
kerakoll/geolite.caveat: The sheet quotes per centimetre and the rate here is that divided by ten. Minimum thickness 2 mm, maximum thickness per layer 40 mm.

kerakoll/geolite-magma.source: COVERAGE: approximately 19 kg/m2 per cm of thickness.
kerakoll/geolite-magma.caveat: The sheet quotes per centimetre and the rate here is that divided by ten. Minimum thickness 10 mm, maximum 60 to 100 mm according to the type of work. For thicker layers the sheet mixes in Ghiaia 3.6 gravel, which changes the rate.

kerakoll/keracem.source: Coverage: approx. 2 to 2.5 kg/m2 per cm of thickness, which is 0.2 to 0.25 kg/m2 per mm. The sheet quotes per centimetre and the division is ours.
kerakoll/keracem.caveat: This is the binder only, not the finished screed. The figure holds at the sheet's own dosage of 200 kg of Keracem per cubic metre of sand for ceramic and stone, and at least 250 for hardwood; the sand is a separate order and is most of the material. The sheet says heavy or concentrated loads must be calculated case by case. The 20 to 80 mm bounds are the sheet's bonded screed range and the 50 mm default is the thickness its own waiting times are quoted at. Mapei Topcem, the equivalent in that range, is treated the same way on this site.

kerakoll/keracem-pronto.source: COVERAGE: approximately 16 to 18 kg/m2 per cm of thickness.
kerakoll/keracem-pronto.caveat: The sheet quotes per centimetre and the rate here is that divided by ten. Printed thicknesses are 20 to 80 mm for a bonded screed and 40 to 80 mm for a floating screed, with a maximum of 80 mm.

kerakoll/keracem-prontoplus.source: COVERAGE: approximately 16 to 18 kg/m2 per cm of thickness.
kerakoll/keracem-prontoplus.caveat: The sheet quotes per centimetre and the rate here is that divided by ten. Printed thicknesses are 20 to 80 mm for a bonded screed and 40 to 80 mm for a floating screed, with a maximum of 80 mm.

kerakoll/metric-track.source: COVERAGE: approximately 19 kg/m2 per cm of thickness.
kerakoll/metric-track.caveat: The sheet quotes per centimetre and the rate here is that divided by ten. Minimum thickness 10 mm, maximum 60 to 100 mm according to the type of work. For thicker layers the sheet mixes in Ghiaia 3.6 gravel, which changes the rate.

mapei/mapefer.reason: The sheet quotes 120 g per metre of Mapefer for 8 mm diameter rebar and 240 g per metre for 16 mm diameter rebar, both at a 2 mm thick coat. That is a rate per metre of reinforcement that scales with the bar diameter, and no model here holds a figure that varies by bar size, so forcing it into an area or a length calculator would produce a number the sheet never printed. Count the metres of exposed rebar, read the rate for the nearest bar diameter above, and order in 2 kg buckets (A plus B).

mapei/mapefinish.source: CONSUMPTION: 2.2 kg/m2 per mm of thickness.

pack.label: unit (A 25 kg bag plus B 4 kg tank)

mapei/mapefinish.caveat: The sheet applies up to 2 mm per layer and says the total skimming thickness must never exceed 4 mm, so the default here is the maximum for one layer. The sheet prints no minimum, so the 1 mm lower bound is an input limit.

mapei/mapegrout-gunite-300-af-me.source: CONSUMPTION: approximately 20 kg/m2 per cm of thickness, approximately 22 kg/m2 per cm if considering 10% rebound.
mapei/mapegrout-gunite-300-af-me.caveat: The sheet quotes per centimetre and the rate here is that divided by ten. Add ten percent for rebound on sprayed work, which is the 22 kg/m2 per cm figure the sheet also prints. Applied in thicknesses up to approximately 10 to 15 cm per layer; the sheet prints no minimum, so the 10 mm lower bound is an input limit.

mapei/mapegrout-me05.caveat: The sheet publishes a yield in litres of mortar per bag rather than a rate, so the rate here is 25 kg divided by 12.7 litres, which is 1.97 kg of powder per litre of mortar, and one square metre at one millimetre is one litre. Application thickness 15 to 220 mm.

mapei/mapegrout-me06.caveat: The sheet publishes a yield in litres of mortar per bag rather than a rate, so the rate here is 25 kg divided by 12.3 litres, which is 2.03 kg of powder per litre of mortar, and one square metre at one millimetre is one litre. For gaps from 30 mm to 250 mm, so the default depth is the printed minimum.

mapei/mapegrout-sv-me.caveat: The same sheet also prints a yield of 12.25 litres per 25 kg, which works out at 20.4 kg/m2 at 1 cm, eleven percent below the 23 kg/m2 consumption figure quoted here. The consumption figure is the higher of the two and most likely carries a site allowance. Thickness applied up to 50 mm; the sheet prints no minimum, so the 10 mm lower bound is an input limit.

mapei/mapegrout-t80.caveat: The sheet publishes a yield in litres of mortar per bag rather than a rate, so the rate here is 25 kg divided by 13 litres, which is 1.92 kg of powder per litre of mortar, and one square metre at one millimetre is one litre. Applied at a minimum thickness of 10 mm up to 60 mm in a single layer.

mapei/mapegrout-tx-60-me.caveat: The sheet publishes a yield in litres of mortar per bag rather than a rate, so the rate here is 25 kg divided by 13.0 litres, which is 1.92 kg of powder per litre of mortar, and one square metre at one millimetre is one litre. Applied at a minimum thickness of 10 mm up to 60 mm in a single layer.

mapei/planitop-105-me.source: CONSUMPTION: 1.2 kg/m2 per mm of thickness, depending on the substrate conditions.
mapei/planitop-105-me.caveat: Application thickness 1 to 2 mm per layer, and up to 3 mm for small patch filling, so the default here is the maximum for a normal layer. The same sheet also prints a yield of 14.3 litres per 20 kg, which works out at 1.40 kg/m2 per mm, seventeen percent above the 1.2 kg/m2 consumption figure quoted here. The consumption figure is the one used.

mapei/planitop-110-me.source: CONSUMPTION: 1.2 kg/m2 per mm of thickness, depending on the substrate conditions.
mapei/planitop-110-me.caveat: Maximum application thickness 2 mm, applied 1 to 2 mm per coat and up to 3 mm for small patch filling, so the default here is the printed maximum per coat. The same sheet also prints a yield of 15.3 litres per 20 kg, which works out at 1.31 kg/m2 per mm, nine percent above the 1.2 kg/m2 consumption figure quoted here. The consumption figure is the one used.

mapei/planitop-220-me.source: CONSUMPTION: the average consumption is approx. 1.6 kg/m2 per mm of thickness, depending on the surface substrate conditions.

pack.label: unit (A 17.5 kg bag plus B 5.25 kg drum)

mapei/planitop-220-me.caveat: Applied at a maximum thickness of 0.5 to 2 mm per layer, and up to 10 mm in multiple layers, so the default here is the maximum for one layer. The sheet also prints a yield of 14.21 litres per 22.75 kg unit, which works out at 1.60 kg/m2 per mm and agrees exactly with the consumption figure.

mapei/planitop-400-me.source: CONSUMPTION: 18 kg/m2 per cm of thickness.
mapei/planitop-400-me.caveat: The sheet quotes per centimetre and the rate here is that divided by ten. Applied at a variable thickness between 2 and 30 mm, up to 3 cm per layer.

mapei/planitop-fast-330.source: CONSUMPTION: approx. 1.55 kg/m2 per mm of thickness, 1 cm thick gives 15.5 kg/m2.
mapei/planitop-fast-330.caveat: Thickness of layer, from 3 to 30 mm.

mapei/planitop-g40-me.source: CONSUMPTION: approximately 16 kg/m2 per 10 mm of thickness.
mapei/planitop-g40-me.caveat: The sheet quotes per 10 mm and the rate here is that divided by ten. Applied from a minimum of 10 mm to a maximum of 50 mm per layer, and over 20 mm without formwork only after roughening the surface.

mapei/planitop-hdm-maxi.source: CONSUMPTION: 1.85 kg/m2 per mm of thickness.

pack.label: kit (A 25 kg bag plus B 6.25 kg canister)

mapei/planitop-hdm-maxi.caveat: Applied by trowel or spray in layers up to 25 mm, with the sheet sending layers under 6 mm to Planitop HDM. A Mapegrid reinforced build up is two layers of around 5 to 6 mm each, so about 11 to 12 mm in total.

mapei/planitop-hpc.source: CONSUMPTION: approx. 20 kg/m2 per cm of thickness.
mapei/planitop-hpc.caveat: The sheet quotes per centimetre and the rate here is that divided by ten. Thickness applied up to 40 mm without additional reinforcement mesh; the sheet prints no minimum, so the 10 mm lower bound is an input limit. Component A is supplied in 25 kg bags and must be mixed with 6.5 percent by weight of component B, Fibre HPC, supplied in 6.5 kg boxes, so order the fibres alongside the bags.

mapei/planitop-hpc-floor.source: CONSUMPTION: approx. 21 kg/m2 per cm of thickness.
mapei/planitop-hpc-floor.caveat: The sheet quotes per centimetre and the rate here is that divided by ten. Thickness applied up to 40 mm without additional reinforcement mesh; the sheet prints no minimum, so the 10 mm lower bound is an input limit.

mapei/adesilex-gp.source: CONSUMPTION: 1.80 kg/m2 per mm of thickness.
mapei/adesilex-gp.caveat: An epoxy mortar applied in thicknesses up to 1 cm, including on vertical structures. The sheet prints no minimum, so the 1 mm lower bound is an input limit, and the default is the printed maximum.

mapei/mapefloor-i-360-as.source: CONSUMPTION: max 2.4 kg/m2 of Mapefloor I 360 AS.

tiers.label: Single layer up to 1.5 mm thick, notched spreader or rake
tiers.hint: Electrically conductive self levelling resin layer

mapei/mapefloor-i-360-as.caveat: The sheet says consumption should never exceed 2.4 kg/m2 or the electrical conductivity is compromised, so this is a ceiling and not a range. The layer sits on Primer SN, Copper Band and Primer W-AS N, which are separate products with their own rates.

mapei/mapefloor-pu-406.source: CONSUMPTIONS, 1. As protective and wear resistant layer for car parks.

layers.name: Mapefloor PU 406 (A + B)
Quartz 0.25
Quartz 0.5 or Quartz 0.9 or Quartz 1.2, broadcast in excess

mapei/mapefloor-pu-406.caveat: A layer schedule, not a single rate: only the first line is this product. The sheet prints a second schedule for elastic crack suppressant membranes in Terrazzo resin systems where Mapefloor PU 406 runs 0.5 to 0.8 kg/m2 per layer. It also notes the consumptions are merely indicative and are influenced by the substrate and the temperature.

mapei/mapefloor-pu-410.source: CONSUMPTION: as a waterproof wear resistant membrane layer for Mapefloor Parking System WD.

layers.name: Mapefloor PU 410 (A + B + Mapecolor Paste)
Quartz 0.25 ME
Broadcast in excess with Quartz 0.5 ME or Quartz 0.9 ME or Quartz 1.2 ME

mapei/mapefloor-pu-410.caveat: A layer schedule, not a single rate: only the first line is this product. The printed layers total 5.3 kg/m2 of materials, so quoting the 1.0 kg/m2 line as the whole system understates it. The sheet notes the figures are merely indicative.

mapei/mapefloor-pu-460.source: CONSUMPTION: Mapefloor PU 460, approx. 2.5 kg/m2 to form a 2 mm thick layer.

tiers.label: 2 mm layer, notched trowel then back rolled
tiers.hint: The one thickness the sheet quotes

mapei/mapefloor-pu-460.caveat: The sheet gives one figure for one thickness and asks for at least 2 mm, so it is a rate per square metre rather than a rate per millimetre.

mapei/nivorapid.source: CONSUMPTION: 1.6 kg/m2 per mm of thickness.
mapei/nivorapid.caveat: The sheet is headed for layers from 1 to 20 mm thick and sends thicknesses under 1 mm to Planipatch. Also supplied in 4 x 5 kg packs.

mapei/planiprep-4-lvt.source: CONSUMPTION: consumption of Planiprep 4LVT is approximately 0.08 to 0.1 kg/m2.

tiers.label: Skim over tiled surfaces, filling the joints
tiers.hint: Layers up to 2 mm, down to a feather edge

mapei/planiprep-4-lvt.caveat: A ready to use grout smoother. The sheet quotes a rate per square metre and not a rate per millimetre, because the product fills joints rather than building a layer.

mapei/planiprep-fast-track.source: CONSUMPTION: the consumption rate for Planiprep Fast Track is approximately 1.0 kg/m2 per mm of thickness.
mapei/planiprep-fast-track.caveat: The sheet sets a maximum thickness of 1 cm and prints no minimum, so the 1 mm lower bound here is an input limit rather than a sheet figure.

mapei/ultraplan.source: CONSUMPTION: 1.6 kg/m2 per mm of thickness.
mapei/ultraplan.caveat: Thickness per layer, from 1 to 10 mm. The 3 mm default is a realistic levelling pass, and the sheet asks for at least 3 mm where wood is to be overlaid.

mapei/ultraplan-contract.source: CONSUMPTION: 1.7 kg/m2 per mm of thickness.
mapei/ultraplan-contract.caveat: Thickness per coat, 1 to 10 mm per coat. The sheet asks for at least 3 mm where wooden flooring is to be installed.

mapei/ultraplan-eco-20.source: CONSUMPTION: 1.6 kg/m2 per mm of thickness.
mapei/ultraplan-eco-20.caveat: Thickness per layer, from 1 to 10 mm. The sheet recommends a minimum of 3 mm for areas subject to wheeled service loads.

mapei/ultraplan-maxi.source: CONSUMPTION: 1.7 kg/m2 per mm of thickness.
mapei/ultraplan-maxi.caveat: Thickness per layer, from 3 to 40 mm. The 10 mm default is a realistic single pass within that range.

mapei/ultraplan-trade.source: CONSUMPTION: 1.75 kg/m2 per mm of thickness.
mapei/ultraplan-trade.caveat: Thickness applicable per coat, 3 to 40 mm per coat. The 10 mm default is a realistic single pass within that range.

mapei/ultratop.source: CONSUMPTION: Ultratop used pure, 16.5 to 17.5 kg/m2 per cm of thickness.
mapei/ultratop.caveat: The sheet quotes per centimetre and the rate here is that divided by ten. Printed thickness is 5 to 40 mm, and 10 to 40 mm if the floor is to be polished. The figure is for Ultratop used pure, without added aggregate.

pidilite-puma/paviland-sl-10.source: Approximate yield: 1.5 kg/m2 and mm thickness.
pidilite-puma/paviland-sl-10.caveat: Application thickness from 2 to 10 mm, with a suggested maximum of around 10 mm in a single layer.

pidilite-puma/paviland-sl-10r.source: Approximate yield: 1.5 kg/m2 per mm of thickness.
pidilite-puma/paviland-sl-10r.caveat: The recommended thickness is 2 to 10 mm applied in one coat. The sheet prints the rate with a comma decimal separator, as 1,5 kg/m2.

kerakoll/biocalce-intonaco.source: Coverage Biocalce Intonaco: approx. 13 kg/m2 per cm of thickness
kerakoll/biocalce-intonaco.caveat: The sheet quotes 13 kg/m2 per centimetre, divided by 10 here to give 1.3 kg/m2 per millimetre. Maximum thickness obtainable by coat is approx. 2 cm, so a thicker render is built in layers.

kerakoll/biocalce-intonaco-fino.source: Coverage Biocalce Intonaco Fino: approx. 12 kg/m2 per cm of thickness
kerakoll/biocalce-intonaco-fino.caveat: The sheet quotes 12 kg/m2 per centimetre, divided by 10 here to give 1.2 kg/m2 per millimetre. Maximum thickness obtainable by coat is approx. 2 cm.

kerakoll/biocalce-zoccolatura.source: Coverage Biocalce Zoccolatura: approx. 12 kg/m2 per cm of thickness
kerakoll/biocalce-zoccolatura.caveat: The sheet quotes 12 kg/m2 per centimetre, divided by 10 here. Minimum thickness obtainable is approx. 2 cm and the maximum by coat is approx. 2 cm, so anything thicker is built in layers.

kerakoll/biocalce-intonachino-fino.source: Coverage Biocalce Intonachino Fino: approx. 1.6 kg/m2 per mm of thickness
kerakoll/biocalce-intonachino-fino.caveat: Max thickness approx. 5 mm. The default is the middle of that range, not 1 mm.

kerakoll/biocalce-intonachino-granello.source: Coverage Biocalce Intonachino Granello approx. 1.5 kg/m2 per mm of thickness
kerakoll/biocalce-intonachino-granello.caveat: Max thickness approx. 10 mm. The default is the middle of that range.

kerakoll/biocalce-intonachino-tipo-00.source: Biocalce Intonachino Tipo 00 coverage: approx. 1 kg/m2 per mm of thickness
kerakoll/biocalce-intonachino-tipo-00.caveat: Max thickness approx. 2 mm. On a skim that thin the printed maximum is the job, so it is the default.

kerakoll/rasobuild-eco-extrafino.source: Coverage will be approx. 1.1 kg/m2 per mm of thickness, applied in two coats
kerakoll/rasobuild-eco-extrafino.caveat: Max thickness 2 mm. On a skim that thin the printed maximum is the job, so it is the default.

kerakoll/rasobuild-eco-fino.source: Coverage will be approx. 1.2 kg/m2 per mm of thickness
kerakoll/rasobuild-eco-fino.caveat: Max thickness 5 mm. The default is the middle of that range.

kerakoll/rasobuild-eco-granello.source: Coverage will be approx. 1.3 kg/m2 per mm of thickness
kerakoll/rasobuild-eco-granello.caveat: Max thickness 10 mm. The default is the middle of that range.

kerakoll/rasobuild-eco-top-fino.source: Coverage will be approx. 1.3 kg/m2 per mm of thickness
kerakoll/rasobuild-eco-top-fino.caveat: Max thickness 10 mm. The default is the middle of that range.

kerakoll/rasobuild-eco-top-granello.source: Coverage will be approx. 1.3 kg/m2 per mm of thickness
kerakoll/rasobuild-eco-top-granello.caveat: The sheet prints a maximum thickness of 20 mm and no recommended one. With a grading of 0 to 1.4 mm this is a finishing skim, so the calculator starts at 3 mm; the 1 mm floor and the 3 mm default are the calculator’s, not the sheet’s. The sheet says in terms not to use it for high thickness correction.

kerakoll/biocalce-marmorino.source: Coverage per m2 (kg/m2 at a thickness of 1.5 mm): approx. 1.7 kg
kerakoll/biocalce-marmorino.caveat: The sheet prints coverage of approx. 1.7 kg/m2 at a thickness of 1.5 mm, which is also the maximum thickness obtainable. The 1.13 kg/m2 per mm rate is that figure divided by 1.5, so at the default 1.5 mm the result is the sheet's own 1.7 kg/m2.

kerakoll/biocalce-intonachino-colorato.source: Coverage on finished substrate with Biocalce Intonachino Fino: 0.5 approx. 1.4 kg/m2, 0.7 approx. 1.7 kg/m2, 1.2 approx. 2.5 kg/m2

tiers.label: Biocalce Intonachino Colorato 0.5
tiers.hint: Grain size 0.5 mm, maximum thickness 0.5 mm

tiers.hint: Grain size 0.7 mm, maximum thickness 0.7 mm

tiers.hint: Grain size 1.2 mm, maximum thickness 1.2 mm

kerakoll/biocalce-intonachino-colorato.caveat: The coverage is per grain size, not per millimetre, because the maximum thickness obtainable equals the grain size. Quoted on a substrate already finished with Biocalce Intonachino Fino. Allow approx. 24 hours between a first and second coat.

kerakoll/biocalce-silicato-puro.source: Coverage on finished substrate with Biocalce Intonachino Fino: 1.0 approx. 1.8 kg/m2 per single coat, 1.2 approx. 2.1 kg/m2, 1.5 approx. 2.4 kg/m2

tiers.hint: Grain size 1.5 mm, maximum 1.5 mm per coat

kerakoll/biocalce-silicato-puro.caveat: The figures are per single coat and per grain size, quoted on a substrate already finished with Biocalce Intonachino Fino.

kerakoll/biocalce-fondo.source: Coverage Biocalce Fondo: approx. 0.15 to 0.3 l/m2 per single coat

tiers.label: Per single coat, as the sheet quotes it
tiers.hint: The spread covers substrates of different porosity

kerakoll/biocalce-fondo.caveat: Used undiluted or diluted with water up to 10 percent in volume depending on porosity and degree of absorption. The sheet gives one range and does not split it by dilution.

tiers.label: Per coat, as the sheet quotes it
tiers.hint: The spread covers substrates of different porosity

kerakoll/biocalce-fondo-universale.caveat: The technical table gives 0.15 to 0.25 l/m2 while the abstract on the same sheet states a flat 0.25 l/m2. The table range is used here. The product may be diluted up to 20 percent by volume with clean water according to the porosity of the support.

kerakoll/biocalce-tinteggio.source: Coverage per m2 on support finished with Biocalce Intonachino Fino: approx. 0.2 to 0.3 l/m2 for two coats

tiers.label: Two coats, as the sheet quotes it
tiers.hint: On a support finished with Biocalce Intonachino Fino

kerakoll/biocalce-tinteggio.caveat: The figure already covers two coats, so do not multiply it by a coat count. The first coat is diluted with clean water to a maximum of 40 percent by volume and the second to a maximum of 20 percent. The abstract on the same sheet states a flat 0.3 l/m2 for two coats.

kerakoll/rasobuild-eco-consolidante.source: Coverage per coat approx. 0.2 to 0.4 kg/m2

tiers.label: Per coat, ready to use
tiers.hint: The spread depends on the porosity and the grade of cohesion of the substrate

kerakoll/rasobuild-eco-consolidante.caveat: Supplied ready to use. The sheet tells you to apply a second coat criss crossing the direction of the first, which is why two coats is the default, and allows more layers wet on wet until saturation on highly porous substrates.

kerakoll/biocalce-muratura.reason: The sheet quotes coverage as approx. 1.7 kg per cubic decimetre of mortar, which is a volume and not a rate per square metre. It prints no bed thickness, no perpend width and no block size, so every dimension a volume calculator would ask for would be ours rather than the sheet's. Take the mortar volume off the drawing from the block size and the bed and perpend you are building to, then multiply the litres by 1.7 kg. One 25 kg bag makes about 14.7 litres of mortar at that rate.

kerakoll/biocalce-muratura-fino.reason: The sheet quotes coverage as approx. 1.7 kg per cubic decimetre of mortar, which is a volume and not a rate per square metre. It prints no bed thickness, no perpend width and no block size, so every dimension a volume calculator would ask for would be ours rather than the sheet's. Take the mortar volume off the drawing from the block size and the bed and perpend you are building to, then multiply the litres by 1.7 kg. One 25 kg bag makes about 14.7 litres of mortar at that rate. The fine 0 to 1.5 mm grading is the only thing that separates it from Biocalce Muratura on quantity.

kerakoll/biocalce-pietra.reason: The sheet quotes coverage as approx. 1.7 kg per cubic decimetre of mortar, which is a volume and not a rate per square metre. For pointing it prints no joint width and no joint depth, and for building exposed walls it prints no bed thickness, so a volume calculator would have to invent the section rather than read it off the sheet. Rake out and measure the joints you are filling, or take the bed volume off the drawing, then multiply the litres by 1.7 kg. One 25 kg bag mixed with about 4.5 litres of water makes roughly 14.7 litres of mortar at that rate.

kerakoll/keraplast-p6.reason: A latex additive, not an area product. The sheet doses it at approx. 10 to 30 percent of the weight of the cement, and for a slurry key at 1 part Keraplast P6 to 1 part water to 2.5 parts cement.

mapei/monofinish.source: CONSUMPTION: 1.4 kg/m2 per mm of thickness
mapei/monofinish.caveat: Maximum applicable thickness per coat is 2 to 3 mm, so the default is the middle of that range. A thicker build is more than one coat and the quantity scales with the total thickness.

mapei/primer-g.source: CONSUMPTION: the consumption of Primer G depends on the porosity and absorption of the surface. Normal consumption is between 0.08 and 0.15 kg/m2
mapei/primer-g.caveat: The sheet gives a dilution for each use: neat on gypsum based substrates, 1:1 with water on cementitious substrates and between smoothing layers, 1:2 as an anchoring coat for gypsum plasters and 1:3 under wallpaper adhesives. It does not say which dilution the consumption range belongs to, so the figure is treated as product as supplied, which is the safe side for ordering. Also available in 10 kg and 5 kg drums and 1 kg bottles. The sheet prints a single range of 0.08 to 0.15 and no substrate table, so the calculator offers the range rather than splitting it into rows the manufacturer never published.

mapei/eco-prim-grip-plus.source: CONSUMPTION: consumption varies between 0.20 and 0.30 kg/m2 according to the absorption of the substrate
mapei/eco-prim-grip-plus.caveat: Ready to use, no dilution is required. Also available in 10 kg, 5 kg and 1 kg drums. The sheet prints a single range of 0.2 to 0.3 and no substrate table, so the calculator offers the range rather than splitting it into rows the manufacturer never published.

mapei/eco-prim-t-plus.source: CONSUMPTION: consumption varies from 30 to 150 g/m2, depending on the porosity of the substrate and on how it is applied
mapei/eco-prim-t-plus.caveat: A fivefold spread, so the substrate choice matters more here than on any other primer. The sheet applies it diluted up to 1:4 with water on cementitious substrates, up to 1:2 on anhydrite and gypsum, and undiluted or 1:1 on existing ceramic, natural stone, wood and old adhesive residues. Also available in 10 kg and 5 kg jerrycans. The sheet prints a single range of 0.03 to 0.15 and no substrate table, so the calculator offers the range rather than splitting it into rows the manufacturer never published.

mapei/ultratop-base-coat.source: CONSUMPTION: 50 to 80 g/m2, depending on the porosity and absorption of the substrate
mapei/ultratop-base-coat.caveat: Supplied ready to use. The sheet says do not dilute the product. The sheet prints a single range of 0.05 to 0.08 and no substrate table, so the calculator offers the range rather than splitting it into rows the manufacturer never published.

mapei/silancolor-primer.source: CONSUMPTION: consumption is heavily influenced by the absorbency level of the substrate. In normal conditions, consumption rate is approx. 0.10 to 0.15 kg/m2
mapei/silancolor-primer.caveat: Ready to use. The sheet allows dilution with water up to 50 percent, which stretches the coverage of a drum but is not given a separate consumption figure. The sheet prints a single range of 0.1 to 0.15 and no substrate table, so the calculator offers the range rather than splitting it into rows the manufacturer never published.

mapei/silancolor-primer-plus.source: CONSUMPTION: in normal conditions, consumption rate is approx. 0.10-0.15 kg/m2. The sheet prints one range and no substrate table.
mapei/silancolor-primer-plus.caveat: Ready to use. The sheet allows dilution with water up to 50 percent, which stretches the coverage of a drum but is not given a separate consumption figure. Also available in 2 kg drums.

mapei/mapecoat-i-600-w.source: CONSUMPTION: 0.15 to 0.50 kg/m2. The real consumption depends on the absorption of the substrate, its roughness, kind of dilution, method of application

pack.label: kit, 2.3 kg part A plus 3.6 kg part B

mapei/mapecoat-i-600-w.caveat: A better than threefold spread, so the substrate choice carries the answer. The sheet dilutes it with water by weight to suit the use: 1:1 as a primer for Mapefloor I 500 W, 1:0.5 before Mapefloor Urban System, and 1:1 up to 1:5 as an adhesion primer on concrete depending on the absorption of the substrate. Also available as an 11.8 kg kit. The sheet prints a single range of 0.15 to 0.5 and no substrate table, so the calculator offers the range rather than splitting it into rows the manufacturer never published.

mapei/mapecoat-tns-primer-epw.source: CONSUMPTION: considering a homogeneous substrate, 0.1 to 0.2 kg/m2 (diluted product)

pack.label: unit, 2 kg part A plus 8 kg part B

tiers.label: Diluted 1:0.5 with water, as the sheet applies it
tiers.hint: The consumption rate is heavily influenced by the absorption and roughness of the substrate and by the application method

mapei/mapecoat-tns-primer-epw.caveat: The printed figure is of the diluted product. Components A and B are mixed and then diluted with water in a ratio of 1:0.5, so one square metre at 0.2 kg of diluted primer is about 0.13 kg of supplied product. Ordering against the printed figure leaves a margin rather than a shortfall. Do not dilute in any other ratio than the one on the sheet.

mapei/mapefloor-cpu-primer.source: CONSUMPTION: Mapefloor CPU+/Primer approx. 0.3 to 0.4 kg/m2. The consumption is influenced by the roughness and absorption of the substrate
mapei/mapefloor-cpu-primer.caveat: Mapefloor CPU+/Primer is batched from three components, A at 2 kg, B at 2.16 kg and the primer part C at 2.5 kg, so the order is made up in kits rather than in single drums. The sheet prints a single range of 0.3 to 0.4 and no substrate table, so the calculator offers the range rather than splitting it into rows the manufacturer never published.

mapei/mapeproof-sa-primer.source: CONSUMPTION: ca 200 g/m2, depending on the absorption rate of the substrate

tiers.label: As supplied, ready to use
tiers.hint: The sheet gives one figure and names substrate absorption as the reason it varies

mapei/mapeproof-sa-primer.caveat: Supplied ready to use. Mix the contents of the container before use and do not dilute with solvent.

pack.label: unit, 1.5 kg part A plus 0.5 kg part B

tiers.label: Impregnation coat, as the sheet quotes it
tiers.hint: Parts A and B mixed 3 to 1 by weight

mapei/mapewrap-primer-1.caveat: The impregnation is usually carried out in a single coat. On a very porous substrate the sheet asks for a second coat once the first has been completely absorbed.

kerakoll/keradur.source: Coverage approx. 0.5 to 2 kg/m2, applied using a brush or sprinkler in accordance with the absorbency of the substrate

tiers.label: Low absorbency substrate
tiers.hint: Dense, smooth or already sealed surfaces. The lower end of the printed range.

tiers.label: Absorbent substrate
tiers.hint: Porous plaster, render, screed or blockwork. The upper end of the printed range.

kerakoll/keradur.caveat: A fourfold spread tied directly to absorbency, so the substrate choice is the whole answer here. Ready to use. On highly absorbent substrates the sheet asks for several coats, waiting until the previous coat has dried. Also available in 5 kg cans.

kerakoll/primer-uni.caveat: Ready to use, and the sheet sets the dilution by substrate: as is on non absorbent substrates and as a surface insulator on compact gypsum or anhydrite, up to 1:2 with clean water on compact low absorption substrates, up to 1:3 on powdery gypsum or anhydrite followed by a second coat as is, and up to 1:4 where the job is to bind dust. Also available in 5 kg buckets. The sheet prints a single range of 0.1 to 0.2 and no substrate table, so the calculator offers the range rather than splitting it into rows the manufacturer never published.

kerakoll/keragrip-pulep.source: Coverage approx. 30 ml/m2, applied with a cotton cloth on smooth, compact, non absorbent substrates

tiers.label: Single coat with a cloth, as the sheet quotes it
tiers.hint: Smooth, compact, non absorbent substrates before laying reactive adhesives

kerakoll/keragrip-pulep.caveat: Ready to use and applied in a single coat. For priming expansion and deformation joints the sheet gives a different basis, approx. 1 tin per 400 m of a 20 x 10 mm joint. Also available in 10 litre drums.

kerakoll/kerarep.source: Technical Data: Coverage approx. 1.7 kg per litre. Maximum permitted width 3 mm. Specific weight of the mixture 1.7 kg/dm3. Pack: Part A bucket 1 kg / Part B tube 0.03 kg / Part C 20 metal staples.

pack.label: kit, 1 kg part A plus 0.03 kg part B plus 20 staples

kerakoll/kerarep.caveat: The 3 mm width is the sheet's own maximum permitted width, so it is the widest gap this product may be used in and not an average. The 20 mm depth is a bound we supply and the sheet does not print: it asks only that the casting compound penetrate at least two thirds of the thickness of the screed, so set the depth from the screed you are working on and from the cuts made across the crack every 15 to 30 cm.

pidilite-puma/paviland-primer-r.source: Performance: approx. 100 g/m2 at 1:3 dilution, approx. 200 g/m2 at 1:1 dilution

tiers.label: Diluted 1:3 with water
tiers.hint: The first coat of the two step process on medium to highly porous substrates

tiers.label: Diluted 1:1 with water
tiers.hint: Moderately absorbent or non porous surfaces, and the second coat of the two step process

pidilite-puma/paviland-primer-r.caveat: The 1:1 row is the default because the sheet pairs it with moderately absorbent and non porous surfaces and with the second coat on porous ones. A full two step prime on a highly porous substrate is the 1:3 coat plus the 1:1 coat, about 300 g/m2 in total.

pidilite-puma/paviland-primer-ceramic.source: Coverage 125 g/m2, applied as a thin even coat with a medium pile roller

tiers.label: Single coat by medium pile roller
tiers.hint: Avoid over application and ensure no puddles form

pidilite-puma/paviland-primer-ceramic.caveat: The primer must not be diluted. If the primed surface is left exposed for more than 48 hours or becomes dusty, a fresh coat is required.

pidilite-puma/paviland-primer-epoxy.source: Approximate yield: 1st coat 400 g/m2 when applied with roller, 2nd coat 250 g/m2 when applied with roller

pack.label: kit, 7.15 kg part A plus 2.85 kg part B

tiers.label: First coat, by roller
tiers.hint: 400 g/m2, depending on substrate texture, then 8 to 10 hours cure

tiers.label: Second coat, by roller
tiers.hint: 250 g/m2 once the first coat has dried

pidilite-puma/paviland-primer-epoxy.caveat: The two coats carry different rates, so price them one at a time. A full two coat system is about 650 g/m2 of primer. While the second coat is still wet the sheet broadcasts Paviland aggregate at 2 to 2.5 kg/m2 until fully saturated, which is a separate product.

mapei/planicrete-sp.source: APPROXIMATE COVERAGE: A. slurry bond coat or spatter-dash coat 0.3 kg per m2. B. floor screed and wall plaster 1 kg per m2 of 20 mm thickness. C. tile adhesive 0.5 to 1 kg per m2

tiers.label: Slurry bond coat or spatter-dash coat
tiers.hint: Mixed 1 part Planicrete SP to 1 part Portland cement

tiers.label: Floor screed and wall plaster
tiers.hint: Per m2 of 20 mm thickness. Double it at 40 mm

tiers.label: Tile adhesive
tiers.hint: Planicrete SP diluted 1:3 with water and gauged into 4 parts Keracrete Powder

mapei/planicrete-sp.caveat: Pick the use before reading a number: the three uses on this sheet differ by more than three times. The floor screed and wall plaster figure is quoted per 20 mm of thickness and scales with it, so at 40 mm it is 2 kg/m2. Never use Planicrete SP neat as a slurry, always mix it with Portland cement. Also available in 5 kg drums.

mapei/adesilex-pg2.source: CONSUMPTION: 1.65 to 1.75 kg/m2 per mm of thickness

pack.label: kit, 4.5 kg part A plus 1.5 kg part B

mapei/adesilex-pg2.caveat: The sheet says the sufficient thickness to obtain an excellent bonding strength is approximately 1 to 2 mm, so the default is the middle of that range. The mix can be applied up to 1 cm in a single layer on vertical structures.

mapei/adesilex-pg2-tg.source: CONSUMPTION: 1.71 kg/m2 per mm of thickness

pack.label: kit, 4.5 kg part A plus 1.5 kg part B

mapei/adesilex-pg2-tg.caveat: The sheet prints general reprofiling over large areas up to 3 mm, which is the default here, and allows thicknesses up to 1 cm in a single layer on vertical structures.

mapei/adesilex-pg4.source: CONSUMPTION: 1.60 to 1.65 kg/m2 per mm of thickness

pack.label: kit, 4.5 kg part A plus 1.5 kg part B

mapei/adesilex-pg4.caveat: The sheet says the correct thickness to guarantee a good bond between the two parts is approximately 1 to 2 mm, so the default is the middle of that range. Also available in 30 kg and 2 kg kits.

mapei/planicrete.reason: Dosage follows the use, so the sheet's own table is the answer rather than a single rate. Planicrete to water and the consumption of Planicrete in g/m2 per mm of thickness: bonding screeds 10 to 35 mm, 1:3, 40 to 50. Floating screeds over 35 mm, 1:4, 30 to 40. Renders, 1:4, 60 to 70. Renders with Nivoplan, 1:5, 70 to 80. Scratch-coat layers for renders, 1:1, 220 to 230. Filler mortar, 1:2.5, 50 to 60. Bonding slurry, 1:1, 300 to 310.

mapei/mapewrap-21.reason: Consumption depends on the type of fabric and the sheet prints a separate g/m2 table for carbon, glass and basalt MapeWrap fabrics, running from 800 to 900 g/m2 for BI-AX 230 up to 2700 to 2800 g/m2 for UNI-AX 1200. Pick the fabric on the sheet's table rather than from an average.

mapei/mapewrap-31.reason: Consumption depends on the type of fabric and the sheet prints a separate g/m2 table for each MapeWrap fabric range, running from about 900 to 1000 g/m2 on the lightest unidirectional carbon fabrics upward. Pick the fabric on the sheet's table rather than from an average.

mapei/mapewrap-31-sp.reason: Coverage depends on the type of fabric, unidirectional, bi-directional or quadri-directional, and on the height. The sheet gives only an estimate, approx. 950 g/m2 based on presaturation of a 900 g fibre sheet, so the fabric being used has to be named before a quantity is quoted.

mapei/dynamon-mr-2100.label: 0.8 to 2.5 litre per 100 kg of total cementitious material
mapei/dynamon-mr-2100.source: DOSAGE: the normal recommended dosage rate of Dynamon MR2100 is 0.8 to 2.5 litre per 100kg of total cementitious material
mapei/dynamon-mr-2100.caveat: The dose is against the total cementitious material, so the cement plus any fly ash, silica fume or GGBS in the mix, not the cement on its own. The sheet says other dosages may be considered according to the site conditions and mix constituent properties. Supplied in 200 litre drums, 1000 litre IBCs and in bulk on request.

mapei/dynamon-mr-3000.label: 0.5 to 2.5 litre per 100 kg of total cementitious material
mapei/dynamon-mr-3000.source: DOSAGE: the normal recommended dosage rate of Dynamon MR3000 is 0.5 to 2.5 litre per 100kg of total cementitious material
mapei/dynamon-mr-3000.caveat: The dose is against the total cementitious material, so the cement plus any fly ash, silica fume or GGBS in the mix, not the cement on its own. The sheet says other dosages may be considered according to the site conditions and mix constituent properties. Supplied in 200 litre drums, 1000 litre IBCs and in bulk on request.

mapei/dynamon-sr-1200.label: 0.5 to 2.0 litres per 100 kg of total cementitious material
mapei/dynamon-sr-1200.source: DOSAGE: typical dosage rates range from 0.5 to 2.0 liters/100 kg of total cementitious material
mapei/dynamon-sr-1200.caveat: The sheet says the optimum dosage for a given job should be determined by site trials using the selected cement, cement replacement materials and aggregates, and that other dosage rates may be considered subject to trials. The dose is against the total cementitious material, not the cement on its own. Supplied in 200 litre drums, 1000 litre IBC containers and in bulk upon request.

mapei/dynamon-sr-2400.label: 0.5 to 1.5 litre per 100 kg for normal concrete, 0.8 to 2.0 for high performance concrete
mapei/dynamon-sr-2400.source: TYPICAL DOSAGE: for normal concrete 0.5 to 1.5 l/100 kg of total cementitious content, for high performance concrete 0.8 to 2.0 l/100 kg of total cementitious content
mapei/dynamon-sr-2400.caveat: The sheet prints two dosages and this range spans both of them: normal concrete takes 0.5 to 1.5 litre per 100 kg of total cementitious content and high performance concrete 0.8 to 2.0. The optimum has to be figured out by site trials using the selected cement, mineral additions and aggregates. Normally supplied in bulk, and on request in 200 litre drums and 1000 litre totes.

mapei/mapeair-foam.reason: Mapeair Foam is a foaming agent for lightweight concrete and the sheet publishes no dose against the cement, the concrete or the bag. It works in volume of foam instead: one litre of the admixture diluted in 50 litres of water and blown at 3 bar produces around 1000 litres of stable foam at a density of 50 plus or minus 5 kg/m3. How much of that foam a given mix takes depends on the plastic density being aimed at, which the sheet does not tabulate, and it says in terms that the dosage for a specific job has to be determined by trials carried out on site. Supplied in 5 litre and 25 litre jerrycans, 200 litre drums and 1000 litre mega drums.

mapei/mapeair-la-p.label: one 0.5 kg bag per cubic metre of mix
mapei/mapeair-la-p.source: CONSUMPTION, average dosage: 1 0.5 kg bag per cubic metre of mix
mapei/mapeair-la-p.caveat: The sheet prints one average dosage and no range. Its own example mixture for flowable fills lists 0.5 kg/m3 of Mapeair LA/P against 100 kg of cement, 150 to 180 kg of water and 1,400 kg of aggregate. The bags are water soluble and come in boxes of 30, so 30 bags is one box. For light weight concrete below 900 kg/m3 the sheet says the product has to be mixed in water and stirred through a mechanical foam generator, and that the foam volume produced varies with the dosage, the amount of water and the type of generator.

mapei/mapequick-af-70.label: 3 to 10 kg per 100 kg of cement
mapei/mapequick-af-70.source: CONSUMPTION, dosage in weight: from 3 to 10 kg per 100 kg cement
mapei/mapequick-af-70.caveat: A shotcrete accelerator, added at the nozzle during the spraying phase and never directly into the cement mixer. The sheet says not to use it with ordinary concrete, and that the setting time and strength gain achieved vary with the dosage, the type and amount of cement, its aging and the water binder ratio used. Supplied in 274 kg drums and 1288 kg IBCs, with bulk quantities on request.

mapei/mapetard-rcc-me.label: 1 to 6 litres for each cubic metre of mix to be batched
mapei/mapetard-rcc-me.source: DOSAGE: generally, the dosage in volume of Mapetard RCC ME is between 1 and 6 litres for each cubic metre of mix to be batched
mapei/mapetard-rcc-me.caveat: The dose depends on the mix composition, in particular on the amount of water and cement in it, and on how long the workability has to be held, which the sheet puts at up to 72 hours after batching. Different dosages must be tested through concrete trials first. Added during the batching, generally as the last ingredient and in any case after the water and the cement. Supplied in bulk, in 1000 litre IBCs and in 25 kg jerrycans, and because the jerrycan is quoted by weight and the dose by volume no pack count is offered here.

mapei/mapesil-ac.source: CONSUMPTION: consumption varies depending on the joint size. The printed expansion joint table runs from 25 ml per linear metre at 5 x 5 mm to 1000 ml at 50 x 20 mm, with a 310 ml cartridge yielding 3.1 m at 10 x 10 mm.

profiles.label: Butt or expansion joint, rectangular section

mapei/mapesil-ac.caveat: Width times depth in millimetres is the millilitres per linear metre exactly, with no constant. All 10 printed expansion joint rows, all 7 printed fillet rows and all 10 printed 310 ml cartridge yields reproduce, 27 of 27 cells. The depth is the sheet's own: equal to the width up to 10 mm, 10 mm for widths of 10 to 20 mm, then half the width capped at 20 mm. Cartridges come in boxes of 12. On absorbent substrates the sheet also calls for Mapei Primerseal A or M at 100 to 300 g/m2, at a primer volume of no more than 5 percent of the sealant volume.

mapei/mapesil-lm.source: JOINT SIZING AND CONSUMPTION: metres of product per cartridge, 12 m at 5 x 5 mm, 3 m at 10 x 10 mm, 1.5 m at 20 x 10 mm and 0.4 m at 40 x 20 mm.

profiles.label: Butt or expansion joint, rectangular section

mapei/mapesil-lm.caveat: The printed yields are 310 ml divided by the joint section: all 8 butt rows reproduce, and 3 of the 4 fillet rows. The 15 mm fillet row prints 3 m where the section gives 2.8 m, so that one row of the sheet is about 8 percent optimistic. Cartridges come in self supporting boxes of 12.

mapei/mapeflex-pu-45-ft.source: CONSUMPTION TABLE: linear metres per cartridge, 12 m at 5 x 5 mm, 3 m at 10 x 10 mm, 2 m at 15 x 10 mm, 1.5 m at 20 x 10 mm, 0.9 m at 25 x 12.5 mm and 0.6 m at 30 x 15 mm.

profiles.label: Butt or expansion joint, rectangular section

mapei/mapeflex-pu-45-ft.caveat: Also supplied in 600 ml cartridges, boxes of 20, where the same table prints 24, 6, 4, 3, 1.9 and 1.3 m. All 6 printed rows of the 300 ml column and all 6 of the 600 ml column reproduce as the pack size divided by the joint section, rounded down. Used as an adhesive instead of a sealant, the sheet gives no rate at all: it depends on whether the product is applied in beads or spots.

mapei/mapeflex-ms-45.source: CONSUMPTION TABLE: linear metres per cartridge, 12 m at 5 x 5 mm, 3 m at 10 x 10 mm, 2 m at 15 x 10 mm, 1.5 m at 20 x 10 mm, 0.9 m at 25 x 12.5 mm and 0.6 m at 30 x 15 mm.

profiles.label: Butt or expansion joint, rectangular section

mapei/mapeflex-ms-45.caveat: Also supplied in 600 ml sausages, boxes of 20. All 6 printed rows of the 300 ml table reproduce as 300 divided by the joint section, rounded down. Used as an adhesive instead of a sealant, the sheet gives no rate at all: it depends on whether the product is applied in beads or spots.

mapei/mapeflex-ms-crystal.source: CONSUMPTION TABLE: linear metres per cartridge, 12 m at 5 x 5 mm, 3 m at 10 x 10 mm, 2 m at 15 x 10 mm, 1.5 m at 20 x 10 mm, 0.9 m at 25 x 12.5 mm and 0.6 m at 30 x 15 mm.

profiles.label: Butt or expansion joint, rectangular section

mapei/mapeflex-ms-crystal.caveat: All 6 printed rows reproduce as 300 divided by the joint section, rounded down. Supplied in boxes of 12 cartridges. Used as an adhesive instead of a sealant, the sheet gives no rate at all: it depends on whether the product is applied in beads or spots.

mapei/mapeflex-pu-s25.source: CONSUMPTION FOR 600 ML CARTRIDGE: 24 m at 5 x 5 mm, 6 m at 10 x 10 mm, 5.3 m at 15 x 7.5 mm, 3 m at 20 x 10 mm, 1.9 m at 25 x 12.5 mm and 1.3 m at 30 x 15 mm.

profiles.label: Butt or expansion joint, rectangular section

mapei/mapeflex-pu-s25.caveat: All 6 printed rows reproduce as 600 divided by the joint section. Note the sheet pairs 15 mm wide with only 7.5 mm deep, not the 10 mm its sister products use. Supplied in boxes of 24 sausages.

mapei/mapesil-z-plus.source: COVERAGE TABLE (linear metres per cartridge): butt joint 11 m at 5 x 5 mm, 2.8 m at 10 x 10 mm, 1.4 m at 20 x 10 mm and 0.4 m at 40 x 20 mm.

profiles.label: Butt or expansion joint, rectangular section

mapei/mapesil-z-plus.caveat: All 7 printed butt rows and all 4 printed triangular rows reproduce as 280 divided by the joint section, 11 of 11 cells. The cartridge is 280 ml here, not the 310 ml of the rest of the Mapesil range, and comes in boxes of 12.

mapei/mapeflex-psu-sl-me.source: CONSUMPTION: litres per linear metre, 0.050 for a 10 x 5 mm joint, 0.200 for 20 x 10 mm, 0.800 for 40 x 20 mm and 1.250 for 50 x 25 mm.

pack.label: pack of A plus B (5 litres)

profiles.label: Butt or expansion joint, rectangular section

mapei/mapeflex-psu-sl-me.caveat: All 4 printed cells reproduce exactly: a litre per metre is 1000 ml of joint section, so 20 x 10 mm is 0.200 litres. The sheet allows joints from 5 to 50 mm wide, asks for a 2 to 1 width to depth ratio, and sets minimum depths of 5 mm on metals, glass and other non porous surfaces, 10 mm on all porous surfaces and 20 mm on trafficked joints and joints under hydrostatic pressure. The pouring grade SL ME comes in 5 litre A plus B packs; the gun grade NS ME in 4 litre packs; density is 1.55 to 1.66 kg per litre.

mapei/mapeflex-pu-70-sl.source: CONSUMPTION: consumption of sealant in kg per metre, 0.04 at 5 x 5 mm, 0.15 at 10 x 10 mm, 0.29 at 20 x 10 mm, 0.65 at 30 x 15 mm and 1.16 at 40 x 20 mm, with a density of 1.45 g per cm3.

profiles.label: Butt or expansion joint, rectangular section

mapei/mapeflex-pu-70-sl.caveat: The calculator gives the joint volume in millilitres. The sheet's own kilogrammes are that volume times its printed density of 1.45 g per cm3, and all 8 printed kg per metre cells reproduce that way. It is sold in 10 kg kits of A plus B, for which the sheet prints 276, 69, 46, 34, 22, 15, 11 and 9 metres across those eight joint sizes, so divide the litres by 6.9 for kits. Primer PU60 is a separate line at a tenth of the sealant, 0.013 kg per metre at 10 x 10 mm. The printed rates are theoretical and carry no waste.

mapei/mapeflex-ac4.source: RATIO WIDTH / DEPTH OF THE JOINT: up to 10 mm wide the depth is the same as the width, from 11 to 20 mm the depth is 10 mm in all cases, and above 20 mm the depth is half the width. PACKAGING: 310 ml cartridges, 550 ml soft cartridges and 25 kg buckets.

profiles.label: Butt or expansion joint, rectangular section

mapei/mapeflex-ac4.caveat: This sheet prints no consumption table at all, only the width to depth rule above and the pack sizes, so the quantity here is computed from the joint volume, which is exact arithmetic, and is not a figure quoted from the sheet. The depths come from the sheet's own printed rule. Also available in 550 ml soft cartridges and 25 kg buckets. The sheet caps joint movement at 12.5 percent of the width and asks for a primer coat for a heavy duty seal.

mapei/mapeflex-pu-65.reason: The sheet publishes a density and nothing else: 1.2 kg per litre of components A and B. It prints no joint table and no width to depth rule, so there is no sheet figure to size a joint from. The joint volume in litres, which is the width times the depth in millimetres times the length divided by 1000, times 1.2 gives the kilogrammes, and it is supplied in 10 kg drums of A plus B. It can be extended with Quartz 0.50 up to 1 to 1 by weight, which changes the quantity again.

mapei/mapeproof-swell.reason: The sheet gives one figure rather than a joint table: each 320 ml cartridge forms about 3 linear metres of a 6 to 13 mm diameter swelling bead, so order one cartridge per 3 metres, in boxes of 6. That is a bead laid on a surface, not a joint of a measured width and depth, so there is nothing to calculate from a section.

mapei/mapeflex-express-80-400.source: CONSUMPTION: according to the volume of the hole to be filled. Complete curing, without volume shrinkage, occurs in 24 hours at +23 C. Sizing of the joint: width of joint 5, 10, 15, 20, 30, 40, 50, 75 mm with depth of sealant twice the width. PACKAGING: boxes of 8 600 ml cartridges with 8 static mixers, and 20 l buckets of component A and component B.

pack.label: cartridge, boxes of 8 with static mixers

mapei/mapeflex-express-80-400.caveat: The sheet prints no consumption rate, only that the product is used according to the volume of the hole and that it cures without volume shrinkage, so one litre of mixed product fills one litre of void and the cartridge count follows from that. The 10 by 20 mm section is a printed pair from the sheet's own sizing table, where the ideal depth is twice the width. The sheet also sets a minimum joint width of 6 mm, asks that the expected movement stay under 5 per cent of the joint width, and allows deep joints to be pre-filled with dried Quarzo 1.2 sand below 60 mm or Mapefoam cord above it, which reduces the volume this calculator asks for.

mapei/adesilex-mt-32.source: CONSUMPTION: coverage varies, depending on the evenness of the walls and the back of the wall covering. MAPEI No. 1 trowel from 200 to 250 g/m2, trowel TKB A1/A4 150 to 250 g/m2, roller approx. 200 g/m2, brush approx. 150 g/m2.

tiers.label: MAPEI No. 1 trowel
tiers.hint: The sheet's first named tool for wall coverings

mapei/adesilex-mt-32.caveat: The rows are tools, not sizes, and they are in the sheet's printed order, so the default is the sheet's own first row and also its highest rate rather than the cheapest. The sheet prints the figures in grammes per square metre: 200 to 250 g/m2 is 0.2 to 0.25 kg/m2. Also supplied in 10, 5 and 1 kg buckets. On dusty or absorbent substrates the sheet asks for a primer first, or a coat of Adesilex MT32 itself diluted 1 to 2 with water, which is extra.

mapei/mapecoat-tns-base-coat.source: CONSUMPTION (referred to undiluted product applied on a bituminous conglomerate substrate): porous substrates, first coat 0.4 to 0.6 kg/m2 and second coat 0.3 to 0.5 kg/m2; non porous substrates, first coat 0.2 to 0.4 kg/m2 and second coat 0.1 to 0.3 kg/m2.

tiers.label: Porous substrate, first and second coat
tiers.hint: 0.4 to 0.6 plus 0.3 to 0.5 kg/m2 as printed

tiers.label: Non porous substrate, first and second coat
tiers.hint: 0.2 to 0.4 plus 0.1 to 0.3 kg/m2 as printed

mapei/mapecoat-tns-base-coat.caveat: Each row is the sheet's two printed coats added together, which is how the system is actually laid; the sheet prints the coats separately as 0.4 to 0.6 then 0.3 to 0.5 on a porous substrate and 0.2 to 0.4 then 0.1 to 0.3 on a non porous one. The figures are for undiluted product on a bituminous conglomerate, and the sheet has the binder mixed with 0.1 to 0.5 mm quartz sand and diluted with water before use, which the figures do not include. The default is the porous row because it is the heavier of the two.

mapei/mapecoat-tns-binder.source: CONSUMPTION: approximately 0.9 to 1.2 kg/m2 for application on even substrates with a rubber trowel, referring to concentrated product applied as indicated in the Preparation of the product section.

tiers.label: Even substrate, rubber trowel
tiers.hint: Concentrated product, as prepared on the sheet

mapei/mapecoat-tns-binder.caveat: The sheet opens the same paragraph with a warning that consumption of the first coats is heavily influenced by the absorption and roughness of the substrate, so on a rough or thirsty court the first coat will take more than this.

mapei/mapefloor-cleaner-ed.reason: This is a concentrated detergent for washing a finished resin floor, not a coating, so the sheet publishes a dilution rather than a coverage: use it at 1 to 3 percent, which is 100 to 300 g in 10 litres of water, and increase the concentration on porous or heavily soiled surfaces. It is supplied in 10 kg cans. How far a can goes depends on how much wash water the floor takes, which the sheet does not state.

mapei/mapefloor-decor-700.source: CONSUMPTION: from 1 to 1.5 kg/m2 per layer, depending on the characteristics of the substrate and the type of decorative effect desired.

pack.label: unit of components A and B

layers.name: Repair of cracks, holes and irregularities with Eporip, Mapefloor EP19, Mapefloor JA or Mapefloor JA Fast, where the substrate needs it
layers.rate: no rate printed on this sheet

layers.name: Primer SN mixed with about 20 percent by weight of Quartz 0.5, lightly broadcast with Quartz 0.5 while wet
layers.rate: no rate printed on this sheet

layers.name: First layer, Mapefloor Decor 700 with about 7 percent Mapecolor Paste, diluted with 2 to 20 percent water, then sanded
Second layer, Mapefloor Decor 700, diluted with no more than 10 percent water
Finishing layer, at least two coats of a transparent polyurethane finish from the Mapefloor Finish range
layers.rate: no rate printed on this sheet

layers.name: Optional wax, Mapelux Opaca or Mapelux Lucida over the whole floor
layers.rate: no rate printed on this sheet

mapei/mapefloor-decor-700.caveat: The sheet's system is two layers of Mapefloor Decor 700, so 2 to 3 kg/m2 of this product, for a finished thickness of 1.5 to 3 mm. Supplied in 10 kg units, component A 2 kg plus component B 8 kg.

mapei/mapefloor-ep-19-me.source: CONSUMPTION: Mapefloor EP19 ME 22 kg/m2 per cm of thickness. Primer SN 0.3 to 0.5 kg/m2 depending on the absorption of the substrate.

pack.label: kit of components A, B and C

mapei/mapefloor-ep-19-me.caveat: 22 kg/m2 per cm is 2.2 kg/m2 per mm, and the default of 10 mm is the sheet's own centimetre. The sheet prints no thickness range for the screed, so the 5 to 30 mm bounds on the control are a practical range and not a sheet figure. Primer SN is a separate line at 0.3 to 0.5 kg/m2 and is not in this quantity; it comes in 20 kg kits. The kit is 1.6 kg of A plus 0.8 kg of B plus 24 kg of C and must be mixed whole.

mapei/mapefloor-finish-415-me.source: CONSUMPTION: theoretical consumption 0.3 to 0.8 kg/m2 depending on the selected system.

pack.label: kit of components A and B

mapei/mapefloor-finish-415-me.caveat: Consumption depends on the roughness of the substrate, the surrounding temperature and the type of tool used. The figures are theoretical and are for a substrate between +15 and +35 degrees C; lower temperatures increase both the consumption and the hardening time. The sheet recommends preliminary tests to establish the real rate. The range also moves with the particle size of the broadcast quartz sand under the finish. The kit is 10 kg of A plus 2.5 kg of B.

mapei/mapefloor-finish-450-me.source: CONSUMPTION: theoretical consumption 0.2 to 0.5 kg/m2 depending on the selected system.

pack.label: kit (18.90 kg of A plus 3.60 kg of B)

mapei/mapefloor-finish-450-me.caveat: Consumption depends on the roughness of the substrate, the surrounding temperature and the type of tool used. The figures are theoretical and are for a substrate between +15 and +35 degrees C; lower temperatures increase both the consumption and the hardening time. The sheet recommends preliminary tests to establish the real rate. The sheet lists the two components separately, 18.90 kg of A and 3.60 kg of B, rather than naming a kit weight.

mapei/mapefloor-finish-451.reason: The sheet prints a theoretical consumption of 0.2 to 0.8 kg/m2 and says in the same breath that it depends on the roughness of the substrate and that higher temperatures increase it. A four to one range is not a figure to multiply an area by, so the sheet's own range is shown instead of a calculated quantity. It is supplied as 14 kg of component A plus 6 kg of component B.

mapei/mapefloor-finish-460-me.source: CONSUMPTION: theoretical consumption 0.2 to 0.5 kg/m2 depending on the selected system.

pack.label: kit of components A and B

mapei/mapefloor-finish-460-me.caveat: Consumption depends on the roughness of the substrate, the surrounding temperature and the type of tool used. The figures are theoretical and are for a substrate between +15 and +35 degrees C; lower temperatures increase both the consumption and the hardening time. The sheet recommends preliminary tests to establish the real rate. The kit is 14 kg of A plus 6 kg of B.

mapei/mapefloor-finish-52-w.source: CONSUMPTION: 50 to 150 g/m2 per coat, depending on the characteristics of the substrate.

pack.label: kit of components A and B

mapei/mapefloor-finish-52-w.caveat: The sheet prints 50 to 150 g/m2, which is 0.05 to 0.15 kg/m2, and the figure is per coat. It gives a waiting time between coats of 6 to 24 hours, so two coats is the normal build and the default here. The kit is 4.7 kg of A plus 0.7 kg of B.

mapei/mapefloor-finish-53-w.source: CONSUMPTION: 0.1 to 0.2 kg/m2 per coat, depending on the characteristics of the substrate.
mapei/mapefloor-finish-53-w.caveat: No pack figure is offered because the sheet quotes the rate in kilogrammes but the pack in litres: a 5.5 litre kit, 5.0 litres of component A plus 0.5 litres of B. Converting between the two would need a density the sheet does not print. The sheet describes applying a second coat, with sanding if the maximum waiting time is exceeded, so two coats is the default here.

mapei/mapefloor-finish-58-w.source: CONSUMPTION: 0.1 to 0.2 kg/m2 per coat, depending on the roughness and porosity of the substrate.

pack.label: kit of components A and B

mapei/mapefloor-finish-58-w.caveat: The rate is per coat and the sheet applies the finish in one or two coats, so two is the default here. On cementitious surfaces the sheet requires a primer first, which is a separate product. The kit is 5 kg of A plus 0.5 kg of B.

mapei/mapefloor-finish-htr.source: CONSUMPTION: 0.050 to 0.150 kg/m2 per coat, depending on the type of substrate to be covered.

pack.label: can of components A and B

mapei/mapefloor-finish-htr.caveat: The rate is per coat and the sheet applies it evenly in one or two coats by short pile roller or airless spray, so two is the default here. The can is 7 kg of A plus 3 kg of B.

mapei/mapefloor-i-500-w.source: CONSUMPTION, 1. Multi-layer slip-resistant system, thickness approx. 3 mm (Mapefloor System 51): primer Mapecoat I 600 W 0.15 to 0.50 kg/m2, light broadcast with Quartz 0.5 at 0.5 kg/m2, base layer Mapefloor I 500 W at 2.5 kg/m2, broadcast in excess with Quartz 0.5 at 5 kg/m2, finishing layer Mapefloor I 500 W at 0.7 kg/m2.

pack.label: unit (2 kg of A plus 24 kg of B)

layers.name: Primer, Mapecoat I 600 W (A plus B), if required
Light broadcast with Quartz 0.5
Base layer, Mapefloor I 500 W (A plus B plus Mapecolor Paste)
Broadcast in excess with Quartz 0.5
Finishing layer, Mapefloor I 500 W (A plus B plus Mapecolor Paste)

mapei/mapefloor-i-500-w.caveat: This is System 51, the 3 mm slip resistant build up, and the two Mapefloor I 500 W layers in it come to 3.2 kg/m2 of this product. The sheet prints two other build ups: System 52 at about 5 mm adds an intermediate layer of 2.5 kg/m2 with another 5 kg/m2 broadcast, so 5.7 kg/m2 of this product; and System 53, a smooth self levelling floor 2 to 4 mm thick, is 2 kg/m2 per mm of thickness, so 4 kg/m2 at 2 mm. The 0.15 to 0.50 kg/m2 line is the primer, a different product, and is not this floor's rate. All the rates are theoretical, assume Quartz 0.5 for the broadcast, and move with the condition, absorbency, roughness and temperature of the surface.

mapei/mapefloor-cpu-cove.source: CONSUMPTION: Mapefloor CPU+/COVE approx. 2 kg per litre, depending on the shape and volume of the detail. For covings the typical consumptions are 0.9 kg/m for 3 cm x 3 cm, 1.6 kg/m for 4 cm x 4 cm and 2.5 kg/m for 5 cm x 5 cm.
mapei/mapefloor-cpu-cove.caveat: A coving is a triangular fillet, so the volume per metre is half the product of its two legs in millimetres: a 3 by 3 cm coving is 450 ml per metre, 4 by 4 cm is 800 ml and 5 by 5 cm is 1250 ml. At the sheet's printed 2 kg per litre those are 0.9, 1.6 and 2.5 kg per metre, which is exactly what the sheet prints, 3 of 3 cells. Divide the millilitres by 1000 and multiply by 2 for kilogrammes. No pack is offered because the product is mixed from several packs: component A 2 kg, component B 2.16 kg, component C 25 kg and Mapecolor CPU+ 0.23 kg.

mapei/mapefloor-cpu-mf.source: CONSUMPTION: as scratch coat at 1 mm thickness approx. 1.7 kg/m2; as self-smoothing layer, 3 mm approx. 5.5 kg/m2, 4 mm approx. 7 kg/m2, 6 mm approx. 10 kg/m2.
