mapei/mapefloor-cpu-mf.caveat: Only the sheet's own four printed rows are offered and nothing in between, because the table is not linear and disagrees with the sheet's own 1.7 kg/m2 per mm: 5.5 over 3 mm is 1.83 per mm and 10 over 6 mm is 1.67, an eight percent spread, so interpolating would be our arithmetic rather than Mapei's. Consumption is influenced by the roughness and absorption of the substrate and by site conditions. No pack is offered because the product is mixed from several packs: component A 2 kg, component B 2.16 kg, component C 20 kg bag and Mapecolor CPU+ 0.23 kg, and one batch is two packs of A, two of B, one sack of C and two of Mapecolor.

mapei/mapefloor-cpu-rt.source: CONSUMPTION: Mapefloor CPU+/RT approx. 2.0 kg/m2 per mm thickness. 6 mm thickness approx. 12 kg/m2, 9 mm thickness approx. 18 kg/m2.
mapei/mapefloor-cpu-rt.caveat: The printed rate is linear and reproduces every printed row exactly: 6 mm thickness approx. 12 kg/m2, 9 mm thickness approx. 18 kg/m2. The control is bounded by the thicknesses the sheet prints. Consumption is influenced by the roughness and absorption of the substrate and by site conditions. No pack is offered because the product is mixed from several packs: component A 2 kg, component B 2.16 kg, component C 18.5 kg bag and Mapecolor CPU+ 0.23 kg.

mapei/mapefloor-cpu-ud.source: CONSUMPTION: Mapefloor CPU+/UD approx. 2.0 kg/m2 per mm thickness. 6 mm thickness approx. 12 kg/m2, 9 mm thickness approx. 18 kg/m2, 12 mm thickness approx. 24 kg/m2.
mapei/mapefloor-cpu-ud.caveat: The printed rate is linear and reproduces every printed row exactly: 6 mm thickness approx. 12 kg/m2, 9 mm thickness approx. 18 kg/m2, 12 mm thickness approx. 24 kg/m2. The control is bounded by the thicknesses the sheet prints. Consumption is influenced by the roughness and absorption of the substrate and by site conditions. No pack is offered because the product is mixed from several packs: component A 2 kg, component B 2.16 kg, component C 19 kg bag and Mapecolor CPU+ 0.23 kg.

mapei/mapefloor-cpu-tc.source: CONSUMPTION: as topcoat on concrete or on a Mapefloor CPU+ product, Mapefloor CPU+/TC 0.4 to 1.2 kg/m2 depending on the roughness of the substrate.

tiers.label: Topcoat on concrete or on a Mapefloor CPU+ floor
tiers.hint: The range is the roughness of the substrate

mapei/mapefloor-cpu-tc.caveat: A three to one range, so treat the high end as the figure for a rough or open substrate. No pack is offered because the product is mixed from several packs: component A 2 kg, component B 2.16 kg, component C 2.5 kg bag and Mapecolor CPU+ 0.23 kg.

mapei/mapelux-lucida.caveat: The sheet prints a single figure, 50 g/m2, which is 0.05 kg/m2, and it is per coat: Mapelux Lucida is spread as a first coat and then, once that has dried, a second coat at right angles to it, so two coats is the default here.

mapei/mapelux-opaca.caveat: The sheet prints a single figure, 50 g/m2, which is 0.05 kg/m2, and it is per coat: Mapelux Opaca is spread as a first coat and then, once that has dried, a second coat at right angles to it, so two coats is the default here.

mapei/topcem.source: CONSUMPTION: consumption varies in relation to the thickness of the screed and the dosage of Topcem. For doses of 200 to 250 kg of Topcem per m3 of aggregates, consumption is 2 to 2.5 kg/m2/cm of thickness.
mapei/topcem.caveat: This is the binder only, not the finished screed. 2 to 2.5 kg/m2 per cm is 0.2 to 0.25 kg/m2 per mm, and it holds only at the sheet's dosage of 200 to 250 kg of Topcem per cubic metre of aggregate; the sand is a separate order, silt free and graded 0 to 6 mm. The sheet's own build ups are bonded screeds 10 to 40 mm thick, unbonded screeds at least 40 mm and floating screeds at least 55 mm, all to BS 8204-1:2003, which is where the 10 to 80 mm bounds and the 40 mm default come from.

mapei/topcem-pronto.source: CONSUMPTION: the consumption of Topcem Pronto is about 18 to 20 kg/m2 per cm thickness depending on the compaction degree.
mapei/topcem-pronto.caveat: 18 to 20 kg/m2 per cm is 1.8 to 2.0 kg/m2 per mm, and where in that range a job lands depends on how hard the screed is compacted. This is a ready mixed screed, so unlike Topcem no aggregate is added. The sheet's printed build ups run from 10 to 80 mm, bonded 30 to 80 mm, unbonded 35 to 80 mm, with at least 3 cm over the pipes of a heated screed.

kerakoll/aquaform-d.reason: A painted aluminium drip edging, so there is no consumption figure of any kind on the sheet. It is supplied in 2.7 m bars, with a 12.5 mm tile cover trim, and the external corner, internal corner and connecting piece are ordered as separate pieces. Order by the bar: the running metres of edge divided by 2.7, rounded up, plus the corners counted off the drawing.

kerakoll/aquaform-d-small.reason: A painted aluminium drip edging, so there is no consumption figure of any kind on the sheet. It is supplied in 2.7 m bars, with a 12.5 mm tile cover trim, and the external corner, internal corner and connecting piece are ordered as separate pieces. Order by the bar: the running metres of edge divided by 2.7, rounded up, plus the corners counted off the drawing.

kerakoll/aquaform-d-plus.reason: A painted aluminium drip edging, so there is no consumption figure of any kind on the sheet. It is supplied in 2.7 m bars, with a 12.5 mm tile cover trim, and the external corner, internal corner and connecting piece are ordered as separate pieces. Order by the bar: the running metres of edge divided by 2.7, rounded up, plus the corners counted off the drawing.

kerakoll/aquaform-od-od-plus.reason: A central polypropylene drain, ordered per piece and not by area or metre, so the sheet publishes no consumption rate. The sheet gives the dimensions instead: Aquaform OD has a 45 mm diameter exit hole and a total length of about 400 mm, Aquaform OD Plus a 75 by 75 mm exit hole and a total length of about 460 mm. Count the outlets off the drawing.

kerakoll/aquaform-r.reason: A tool, not a material: a 37 cm wide roller on a stainless steel frame with a handle, used to press the Green-Pro membrane down evenly. There is nothing to calculate. No data sheet is hosted for it either.

kerakoll/aquaform-sd-vd.reason: A central polypropylene drain with a waterproof polyethylene membrane coated both sides in polypropylene fabric, ordered per piece off the drawing rather than by area. No data sheet is hosted for it, so no dimensions or pack figures can be quoted here.

kerakoll/aquastop-120.source: Technical Data: Pack 50 m rolls. Section width approximately 20-80-20 mm (mesh/NBR/mesh). Thickness approximately 0.6 mm. Weight approximately 60 g/m. Instructions for use: the different elements must be connected using the waterproof membrane, overlapping the edges by at least 20 mm.
kerakoll/aquastop-120.caveat: The sheet publishes no consumption rate because nothing is spread: Aquastop 120 is a thermoplastic NBR joint tape bonded into a coat of Aquastop Nanoflex, Nanodefense, Aquastop Fix or Aquastop Nanogum along a wall to floor or fractionising joint, so it is measured by the metre of joint. The 20 mm is the sheet's own figure for connecting one element to the next, and only the lap at the end of each roll is counted here. The internal corner, external corner and flange sections used at corners, edges, pipes and drains are counted off the drawing as pieces, and the waterproofing product it is bedded into is a separate product with its own rate.

kerakoll/aquastop-ar1.source: Technical Data: Roll width approximately 1 m. Roll length 50 m. Instructions for use: lay Aquastop AR1 on the fresh waterproofing gel membrane overlapping the sheets by about 10 cm.
kerakoll/aquastop-ar1.caveat: The sheet publishes no consumption rate because nothing is spread: Aquastop AR1 is an alkali resistant glass fibre mesh pressed into the first coat of Aquastop Nanoflex or Aquastop Flex and covered by the second. What it publishes is the roll and the 10 cm lap, so the quantity here is the length of mesh the area needs once that lap is allowed for. The sheet's weights, about 90 g/m2 uncoated and about 110 g/m2 primed, are there so the weight of mesh in the system can be verified and are not an ordering figure. The transverse laps at the end of each roll are not counted, so on a job made of many short runs order one roll over.

kerakoll/fuga-remove.reason: A hand tool, a tungsten carbide coated scraper for raking out joints of 1 to 5 mm, so there is no consumption figure to publish. It is ordered per piece.

kerakoll/joint.reason: A closed cell expanded polyethylene sub joint layer used to fill static joints and back dynamic ones. No data sheet is hosted for it, so neither a section nor a roll length can be quoted here, and without those there is nothing honest to calculate. It is ordered by the metre once the section is confirmed.

kerakoll/quarzo.source: Coverage: Quarzo 1.3 when used for tacking approx. 1.5 to 2 kg/m2; Quarzo 5.12 when used for tacking approx. 1.5 to 2 kg/m2. Pack: 25 kg bags.

tiers.label: Broadcast for tacking, Quarzo 1.3 or Quarzo 5.12
tiers.hint: The sheet's only figure per square metre

kerakoll/quarzo.caveat: This is the one accessory with a published rate per square metre, and it covers only the broadcast for tacking. Used as a filler the sheet gives ratios instead, which cannot be turned into a rate per square metre without knowing the resin: 1 part resin to 1 part Quarzo 1.3, 1 part adhesive to 5 to 7 parts Quarzo 1.7 depending on the consistency wanted, and as a structural filler in epoxy screeds EP21 at 0.2 kg/m2 per mm with Quarzo 5.12 at 1.6 kg/m2 per mm in a 1 to 8 mix or 2.0 kg/m2 per mm in a 1 to 10 mix. The figures are taken at 23 degrees C and 50 percent relative humidity.

mapei/mapegrout-aggregate.reason: CONSUMPTION: dependant on the type of use, please consult with MAPEI for a technical recommendation. The sheet publishes no rate, because this is a graded aggregate added to a Mapegrout repair mortar to extend it for thicker sections, and how much goes in is set by the mortar's own sheet and the section being repaired. It is supplied in 25 kg bags.

mapei/mapecolor-metallic.reason: CONSUMPTION: the consumption of Mapecolor Metallic varies depending on the aesthetic effect desired, considering approximately 3 percent. It is a metallic pigment dosed by weight into Kerapoxy Easy Design, not spread over an area, and the 90 g sachet is exactly the 3 percent dose for one 3 kg drum. So order one sachet per 3 kg drum of grout and take the grout quantity from the grout's own calculator.

mapei/mapeglitter.reason: CONSUMPTION: the consumption of MapeGlitter varies according to the effect and finish required. The sheet puts no number to it at all, because the glitter is dosed into a grout or resin by eye for the effect wanted. It is supplied in 100 g sachets, in silver and gold.

mapei/mapewrap-c-fiocco.reason: A carbon fibre cord used to form connectors and anchors, so the sheet publishes no rate for the cord itself and no roll width to lap. It comes in various diameters in boxes of 10 m rolls, and every piece is cut to the length the detail needs, which comes off the structural drawing rather than off a floor area. The MapeWrap Primer 1, MapeWrap 11 or 12 and MapeWrap 31 or Mapefix epoxy system that impregnates it and fills the hole are separate products with their own consumption rates.

mapei/mapewrap-c-uni-ax.reason: A unidirectional carbon fibre fabric supplied in cartons of 50 m rolls. The sheet says the range comes in weights from 230 to 1200 g/m2, each with different heights, but it never prints a height, so there is no roll width to lap and no roll calculator can be built from it: the fabric is ordered as metres of the required height off the strengthening drawing. The sheet's consumption table belongs to the epoxy system, not to the fabric: MapeWrap Primer 1 at 250 to 300 g/m2, MapeWrap 11 or 12 levelling mortar at 1500 to 1600 g/m2, and the impregnating resin by fabric weight, for example MapeWrap 21 at 1000 to 1100 g/m2 for a 300 fabric and 1400 to 1500 g/m2 for a 600. Where strips are wrapped around a pillar the sheet requires the ends to overlap by at least 30 cm.

mapei/mapesilent.reason: Mapesilent Panel is a dry soundproofing system of 1 m by 1 m tiles, counted as panels rather than measured off a roll, so no roll calculator fits it. A pallet holds 75 tiles and covers 75 m2, which is one tile per square metre: take the floor area, add the perimeter band and the tape, and count tiles. The joints between tiles are sealed with Mapesilent Tape and the perimeter with Mapesilent Band R, available in 100 and 160 mm wide rolls, both separate products. The sheet's only other figures are a weight of 5.0 kg/m2 to EN 1849-1 and a simplified calculation method that assumes a 100 kg/m2 floating screed with a ceramic floor over it, neither of which is a consumption rate.

mapei/ultrabond-turf-tape.source: PACKAGING: Ultrabond Turf Tape 100 is supplied in 300 m x 0.4 m rolls. TECHNICAL DATA: standard roll length (EN 1848-2) 300 m, width (EN 1848-2) 0.4 m.
mapei/ultrabond-turf-tape.caveat: The sheet publishes no consumption rate because nothing is spread: Ultrabond Turf Tape 100 is a seaming tape laid under the seam between two rolls of synthetic turf, so it is measured by the metre of seam. The sheet prints the roll and no lap between successive pieces of tape. Nothing is added here for a lap between successive pieces, because the sheet prints none: that is a bound the sheet does not print, so allow for it on site. The polyurethane adhesive spread on it is a separate product with its own rate, quoted per linear metre of tape and not per square metre of pitch.

mapei/ultrabond-turf-tape-pro.source: PACKAGING: Ultrabond Turf Tape Pro is supplied in 300 metre rolls. TECHNICAL DATA: length of standard roll 300 m, width 0.3 m.
mapei/ultrabond-turf-tape-pro.caveat: The sheet publishes no consumption rate because nothing is spread: Ultrabond Turf Tape Pro is a polyester non woven seaming tape laid under the seam between two rolls of artificial turf, so it is measured by the metre of seam. The sheet prints the roll and no lap between successive pieces of tape. Nothing is added here for a lap between successive pieces, because the sheet prints none: that is a bound the sheet does not print, so allow for it on site. The Ultrabond Turf polyurethane adhesive spread on it is a separate product with its own rate, quoted per linear metre of tape and not per square metre of pitch.

mapei/mapeband.source: PACKAGING: 50 m rolls of 120 mm total width. 10 m rolls of 120 mm total width. APPLICATION PROCEDURE: joints between Mapeband strips must be sealed with Adesilex LP or Adesilex PVC HP.
mapei/mapeband.caveat: The sheet publishes no consumption rate because nothing is spread: Mapeband is an alkali resistant rubber tape with a felt edge bedded into Mapelastic or a similar membrane along a corner or an expansion joint, so it is measured by the metre of that detail. The figure is for the 50 m roll; a 10 m roll is also made. The sheet says joints between strips are sealed with Adesilex LP or Adesilex PVC HP but does not say by how much they lap. Nothing is added here for a lap between successive pieces, because the sheet prints none: that is a bound the sheet does not print, so allow for it on site. On a movement joint the tape is positioned in an omega shape, which takes more tape per metre of joint than this sum allows, and the sheet does not quantify that either. The 90 and 270 degree angles, the gaskets for 120 x 120 mm and 400 x 400 mm pipes, the 515 x 315 mm T profiles and the 515 x 515 mm cross profiles are counted off the drawing as pieces.

mapei/mapeband-gasket.reason: A preformed gasket from the Mapeband range, counted off the drawing as pieces rather than calculated: the sheet lists gaskets for 120 x 120 mm and 400 x 400 mm pipes, 90 and 270 degree angles, 515 x 315 mm T profiles and 515 x 515 mm cross profiles. A piece seals one pipe or one corner, so the quantity is a count taken from the drawing and there is no length or area to multiply. The 50 m and 10 m rolls of 120 mm band on the same sheet are the Mapeband tape, which has its own roll calculator, and the cementitious membrane the gasket is bedded into is a separate product with its own rate.

mapei/mapeband-pe-120.source: PACKAGING: 10 m and 50 m rolls, 120 mm wide. APPLICATION PROCEDURE: joints between adjacent pieces of Mapeband PE 120 must be bonded using Adesilex PVC HP, solvent resin based adhesive.
mapei/mapeband-pe-120.caveat: The sheet publishes no consumption rate because nothing is spread: Mapeband PE 120 is an alkali resistant band with a polyethylene core embedded in fresh Mapegum WPS along a corner or an expansion joint, so it is measured by the metre of that detail. The figure is for the 50 m roll; a 10 m roll is also made. Nothing is added here for a lap between successive pieces, because the sheet prints none: that is a bound the sheet does not print, so allow for it on site. On an expansion joint the band is positioned in an omega pattern, which takes more band per metre of joint than this sum allows, and the sheet does not quantify that. The 90 and 270 degree angle pieces and the seals for 120 x 120 mm and 425 x 425 mm through holes are counted off the drawing as pieces.

mapei/mapeband-tpe.source: PACKAGING: Mapeband TPE 170 (width 17 cm), 30 m x 17 cm rolls; Mapeband TPE 325 (width 32.5 cm), 30 m x 32.5 cm rolls. APPLICATION: butt joints between two strips of Mapeband TPE must be carried out by overlapping and bonding at least 5 cm of the central part in TPE by either hot welding or cold welding.
mapei/mapeband-tpe.caveat: The sheet publishes no consumption rate because nothing is spread: Mapeband TPE is a thermoplastic elastomer tape bonded over a joint with Adesilex PG1, PG2 or PG4, so it is measured by the metre of joint. The figure is for Mapeband TPE 170, the 17 cm wide tape; Mapeband TPE 325 comes on a 30 m roll 32.5 cm wide and is ordered the same way. Only the 5 cm lap at the end of each roll is counted here. Where high levels of movement are foreseen the sheet says to lay the tape in an omega shape inside the joint, which takes more tape per metre than this sum allows and the sheet does not quantify. The epoxy adhesive it is bedded into is a separate product with its own rate.

mapei/mapeband-flex-roll.source: PACKAGING: width 150/200/300/400/600/800 mm; thickness 2 mm; length of roll 20 m. APPLICATION PROCEDURE: when the pieces of tape are joined by heat welding, overlap the edges by at least 30 mm.
mapei/mapeband-flex-roll.caveat: The sheet publishes no consumption rate because nothing is spread: Mapeband Flex Roll is a 2 mm thick TPE tape bonded over a structural joint in two 1 to 2 mm layers of Adesilex PG1, PG2 or PG4, so it is measured by the metre of joint. The figure is for the narrowest roll, 150 mm wide; the sheet also lists 200, 300, 400, 600 and 800 mm, all on a 20 m roll, and the width comes off the joint detail. Only the 30 mm lap at the end of each roll is counted here. The epoxy it is bedded into is a separate product with its own rate.

mapei/mapeguard-board.reason: An insulation and tiling board, ordered by the panel rather than by area or metre, and the sheet publishes no consumption rate. The printed panel sizes are 60 by 130 cm in 7 and 10 mm and 60 by 260 cm in 10, 20, 30 and 48 mm, packed 16, 16, 8, 8, 6 and 2 panels to a pack. Take the area, divide by the panel area and count packs. The adhesive that fixes it is a separate product with its own rate.

mapei/mapeguard-um-35.source: PACKAGING: 30 m x 1 m rolls. APPLICATION PROCEDURE: waterproofing of joints between the sheets with Mapeband Easy, bonded with Mapeguard WP Adhesive.
mapei/mapeguard-um-35.caveat: The sheet publishes no consumption rate because nothing is spread: Mapeguard UM 35 is an uncoupling and crack bridging membrane bedded in tile adhesive. It prints the roll but no lap, because adjacent sheets are laid up to one another and the joint between them is sealed with Mapeband Easy rather than overlapped, so a 30 m roll covers 30 m2. Nothing is added here for a lap between successive pieces, because the sheet prints none: that is a bound the sheet does not print, so allow for it on site. Cutting around drains, walls and elements passing through the floor is a site allowance the sheet does not quantify. The adhesive above and below the membrane, and the Mapeband Easy and Mapeguard WP Adhesive that seal the joints, are separate products with their own rates.

mapei/mapeguard-wp-200.source: PACKAGING: 1 m x 30 m rolls. 1 m x 5 m rolls. LAYING: the overlap between Mapeguard WP 200 sheets must be minimum 5 cm wide and must be sealed with Mapeguard WP Adhesive.
mapei/mapeguard-wp-200.caveat: The sheet publishes no consumption rate because nothing is spread: Mapeguard WP 200 is a waterproofing and crack bridging membrane bonded into a C2 tile adhesive. What it publishes is the roll and the 5 cm lap, so the quantity here is the length of membrane the area needs once that lap is allowed for. The figure is for the 30 m roll; a 1 m x 5 m roll is also made, which suits a single shower. The transverse laps at the end of each roll are not counted. The adhesive under it, the Mapeguard WP Adhesive that seals the laps and the Mapeguard ST, IC, EC and PC accessories at junctions, corners and pipes are separate products with their own rates.

mapei/mapeplan-t-af.reason: A synthetic roofing membrane, ordered by the roll and not by a consumption rate, which the sheet does not publish. The rolls are 2.10 m wide and either 20 m or 15 m long according to the thickness, 14 rolls to a pallet: take the roof area, divide by the roll area and allow for laps and upstands, which are a design decision and not a sheet figure.

mapei/mapeplan-tu-s.reason: A synthetic membrane for waterproofing tunnels, ordered by the roll rather than from a consumption rate, which the sheet does not publish. It is supplied in 20 m rolls, with longer rolls available on request to suit the tunnel profile or the structure, so the roll area depends on the width agreed for the job and no quantity is offered here.

mapei/mapeproof-al-tape-d10.source: PACKAGING: Mapeproof AL Tape D10 AP is available in 0.1 m x 20 m rolls (box containing 4 rolls). Application of the product: unroll and cut the tape to the length required and place it over the area to be sealed.

pack.label: roll, 0.1 m wide, 4 to a box

mapei/mapeproof-al-tape-d10.caveat: The sheet publishes no consumption rate because nothing is spread: Mapeproof AL Tape D10 AP is a double sided adhesive tape that seals the laps and details of the Mapeproof AL bentonite system, so it is measured by the metre of lap. The sheet prints the roll and no lap between successive pieces of tape. Nothing is added here for a lap between successive pieces, because the sheet prints none: that is a bound the sheet does not print, so allow for it on site. Its weight is a property of the tape and not an ordering figure. The membrane it seals is a separate product with its own roll.

mapei/mapeproof-fbt-tape-600.source: PACKAGING: Mapeproof FBT Tape 600 is available in 0.15 m x 20 m rolls. Application of the product: unroll Mapeproof FBT Tape 600 and, while removing the protective film, bond it over the Mapeproof FBT or Mapeproof FBH membrane.
mapei/mapeproof-fbt-tape-600.caveat: The sheet publishes no consumption rate because nothing is spread: Mapeproof FBT Tape 600 seals the laps and details of the Mapeproof FBT or Mapeproof FBH system, so it is measured by the metre of lap. The sheet prints the roll and no lap between successive pieces of tape. Nothing is added here for a lap between successive pieces, because the sheet prints none: that is a bound the sheet does not print, so allow for it on site. The sheet does add that where a joint is poorly bonded more tape is applied over it, which is a repair and not a quantity. Its weight is a property of the tape and not an ordering figure.

mapei/mapetex-50.source: PACKAGING: Mapetex 50 is available in 20 cm x 25 m rolls and 100 cm x 25 m rolls. APPLICATION PROCEDURE: adjacent sheets of Mapetex 50 must overlap by at least 5 cm at both the longitudinal and transverse junction points.
mapei/mapetex-50.caveat: The sheet publishes no consumption rate because nothing is spread: Mapetex 50 is a non woven polypropylene fabric pressed into the first coat of the liquid membrane and covered by the second. What it publishes is the roll and the lap, so the quantity here is the length of fabric the area needs once the 5 cm lap is allowed for, and the number of rolls that comes to. The figure is for the 100 cm wide roll; the 20 cm x 25 m roll is the detailing roll for forming around construction features and is ordered separately. The transverse laps at the end of each roll are not counted, so on a job made of many short runs order one roll over.

mapei/mapetex-sel.source: PACKAGING: Mapetex Sel is available in 25 m long rolls with a width of 1 m. APPLICATION: adjacent sheets of Mapetex Sel must overlap by at least 5 cm at both the longitudinal and transverse junction points.
mapei/mapetex-sel.caveat: The sheet publishes no consumption rate because nothing is spread: Mapetex Sel is a macro holed non woven fabric laid into the first coat of the waterproofing. What it publishes is the roll and the lap, so the quantity here is the length of fabric the area needs once the 5 cm lap is allowed for, and the number of rolls that comes to. The transverse laps at the end of each roll are not counted, so on a job made of many short runs order one roll over.

mapei/mapegrout-rapido.source: CONSUMPTION: 18 kg/m2 per cm of thickness. The sheet quotes per centimetre and the rate here is that divided by ten.
mapei/mapegrout-rapido.caveat: The sheet prints a maximum layer thickness of 20 to 25 mm and no minimum, so the bounds are yours, not the manufacturer's: the 5 mm lower bound is an input limit taken from the 5 mm surface roughness the sheet asks for on a prepared substrate. Deeper repairs are built up in several layers at intervals of approximately 15 minutes, each worked with a 10 mm notched trowel, so set the thickness to one layer and count the layers. The sheet also prints a mix of 100 kg of powder to 15.5 percent water at a density of 2150 kg/m3, which works out at 18.6 kg/m2 per cm, three percent above the 18 kg/m2 quoted here; the consumption figure is the one used. Add the bonding slurry separately, 1 part powder to 0.24 to 0.25 parts water.

mapei/mapelevel-prowdg.reason: The sheet quotes this system in wedges and spacers, not in kilogrammes or litres, so there is no rate to multiply. Its consumption table gives the indicative number of pieces needed for 10 m2 against the two tile dimensions in centimetres, running from 1,980 pieces per 10 m2 for a 10 by 10 cm tile down to 28 for a 200 by 200 cm slab. The rows do not fall in a straight line, a 30 by 30 cm tile taking 431 pieces per 10 m2 where a 25 by 25 cm takes 312, so read the pair of dimensions off the table rather than interpolating between them. Mapei adds that the consumption is approximate and varies with the tile installation layout and the flatness of the tiles.

mapei/mapetherm-ar1.source: CONSUMPTION: Bonding of insulating boards by bead-and-spot application: approx. 3.0-4.0 kg/m2. Full-surface bonding of insulating boards application: approx. 4.0-6.0 kg/m2. Reinforced levelling coat (recommended thickness 4 mm in 2 coats): approx. 1.3-1.5 kg/m2 per mm of thickness.

tiers.label: Bonding of insulating boards by bead and spot application
tiers.hint: Where the substrate is uneven, with height differences between 5 mm and 10 mm, and at least 40 percent of the board covered with adhesive

tiers.label: Full surface bonding of insulating boards
tiers.hint: Flat substrates, spread over the whole board with a 10 mm notched trowel

tiers.label: Reinforced levelling coat, 4 mm total in two coats
tiers.hint: First coat 2.5 to 3 mm with Mapetherm Net bedded in it, second coat 1 to 1.5 mm after about 24 hours

mapei/mapetherm-ar1.caveat: The first two rows are printed as they stand. The third is the sheet's own rate of 1.3 to 1.5 kg/m2 per millimetre taken at the total reinforced thickness of approximately 4 mm it recommends, a multiplication we performed and not a printed figure; at any other thickness read it back as 1.3 to 1.5 kg/m2 per mm. A full external insulation build needs one bonding row and the levelling row, so quote the two separately and add them. Mapei states that consumption is heavily influenced by the roughness of the substrate and the application method, and that these figures hold for a homogeneous substrate. On masonry rather than board, a levelling coat is capped at 3 mm per coat.

mapei/mapetherm-ar2.source: CONSUMPTION: For bonding panels: spot bonding 2-4 kg/m2; bonding of insulating panels with a uniform layer on the back of the panel using a notch trowel 4-6 kg/m2; smoothing layer 1.4-1.6 kg/m2 per mm of thickness (recommended thickness: 4 mm in 2 coats).

tiers.label: Spot bonding
tiers.hint: Small panels, bonded at various points or only on the edges of the panel

tiers.label: Uniform layer on the back of the panel, notch trowel
tiers.hint: The sheet asks for panels to be bonded on the entire surface, so this is the row a full insulation cladding job is quoted on

tiers.label: Smoothing layer over Mapenet 150, 4 mm in 2 coats
tiers.hint: The printed 1.4 to 1.6 kg/m2 per mm at the sheet's own recommended thickness of 4 mm

mapei/mapetherm-ar2.caveat: The sheet quotes the smoothing layer per millimetre of thickness, 1.4 to 1.6 kg/m2 per mm, and recommends 4 mm in two coats. The third row is those two printed figures multiplied together; at any other skim thickness read 1.4 to 1.6 kg/m2 for each millimetre. Bonding and smoothing are two separate operations on the same wall, so a full cladding job takes a quantity from a bonding row and a second quantity from the smoothing row, not one or the other.

mapei/purtop-500-n.source: CONSUMPTION: The theoretical consumption for a smooth surface with a substrate temperature between +15 C and +25 C is 2.2 kg/m2 every 2.0 mm of thickness. The sheet quotes a total for 2.0 mm, halved here to give the rate per millimetre.

pack.label: kit, component A 225 kg drum plus component B 225 kg drum

mapei/purtop-500-n.caveat: The sheet prints a minimum applied thickness of 2 mm and no maximum, so the upper bound is the calculator's, not the manufacturer's. At the 2 mm default the sum returns the sheet's own printed 2.2 kg/m2, and 2 mm is the thickness every performance figure on the sheet is measured at. The figure is theoretical and for a smooth surface: the sheet says consumption increases on rougher substrates and gives no figure for how much, so a site allowance belongs on top of this.

mapei/ultracare-penetrating-plus-stone-t.source: Approximate Coverage: 1 U.S. pint (473 mL) 25 to 175 sq. ft. (2.32 to 16.3 m2); 1 U.S. qt. (946 mL) 50 to 350 sq. ft. (4.65 to 32.5 m2); 1 U.S. gal. (3.79 L) 200 to 1,400 sq. ft. (18.6 to 130 m2). The sheet quotes an area per pack, not a rate, and all three rows give the same rate, so the gallon row is inverted here into litres per square metre.

tiers.label: Stone, tile, masonry or grout, as printed
tiers.hint: 3.79 litres over 130 m2 at the tight end and over 18.6 m2 at the absorbent end, inverted into litres per square metre. The pint and quart rows invert to the same rate within half a percent.

mapei/ultracare-penetrating-plus-stone-t.caveat: The sheet publishes one rate for every surface and spans porosity inside the range rather than splitting it into rows, so the wide band is the manufacturer's own. It says coverage varies with density, porosity, texture, surface absorption, weather conditions, application method and number of coats, which means the printed range already allows for the second coat that very porous surfaces need one hour after the first. There is no separate coats control for that reason.

mapei/mapefix-ve-sf.reason: Consumption is by the volume of the hole and the sheet prints no rate at all under CONSUMPTION, only the words According to the size of hole to be filled. What sets that volume is a schedule of drilled holes, their diameter, the embedment depth and the diameter of the bar sitting in them, and those are in Mapei attachment tables 2 and 5, published separately on mapei.com and not in this PDF. The sheet says a qualified design engineer must calculate the hole size, the anchor depth and the maximum permitted loads. A round hole with a bar already in it is not a chase of a given length, width and depth, so there is no honest sum to put on this page. Once the engineer has fixed the hole schedule, the resin density of 1.77 g per cubic centimetre turns the empty volume around each bar into kilogrammes. Supplied in 300 ml and 420 ml cartridges, boxes of twelve with twelve static mixers.

mapei/mapestone-tfb-60.source: CONSUMPTION: The consumption of Mapestone TFB 60 is approximately 20 kg/m2 per cm of thickness. The sheet quotes per cm, so the figure is divided by ten to give 2 kg/m2 per mm.
mapei/mapestone-tfb-60.caveat: The sheet prints a minimum application thickness of 40 mm and no maximum, so the upper bound of 70 mm here is ours, not the manufacturer's: it is the top of the sheet's own instruction to spread a 5 to 7 cm thick layer. Above 7 cm the sheet requires 4 to 8 mm gravel to be added at 20 to 25 percent to give the screed structure, which changes what is being ordered. The 20 kg/m2 per cm is the dry powder, not the mixed mortar: adding the 7 to 9 percent gauging water brings it to about 22 kg, which is the 2200 kg/m3 fresh bulk density the sheet prints.

mapei/ultracare-keranet-easy-spray.source: CONSUMPTION: 1 liter of UltraCare Keranet Easy cleans up to 10 m2. PACKAGING: UltraCare Keranet Easy is available in 750 ml bottles with spray.

tiers.label: Ready to use, sprayed and sponged
tiers.hint: Porcelain, ceramic, glass mosaic, quarry tile, terracotta and acid resistant stone

pack.label: trigger spray bottle, printed on the sheet as 750 ml

mapei/ultracare-keranet-easy-spray.caveat: The sheet prints one rate, a litre to ten square metres, and adds that consumption varies with the amount and type of dirt and the kind of surface, so this is the best case and heavy residue will take more. The product is ready to use, a 3 percent solution, so nothing is diluted and the figure is of product, not of mixed solution.

mapei/planigrout-300-me-a-b-c.source: CONSUMPTION: 2.2 kg/m2 per mm of thickness. Emirates edition, document 382-10-2025 (UAE).

pack.label: kit, part A 4.8 kg plus part B 1.8 kg plus part C 2 bags of 22 kg, also a 25.3 kg kit

mapei/planigrout-300-me-a-b-c.caveat: The Emirates sheet prints neither a maximum nor a minimum thickness, so the bounds on this control are ours, not the manufacturer's. The rate agrees with the printed density of the mix, 2200 kg/m3, since one square metre at one millimetre is one litre and 2200 kg/m3 is 2.2 kg per litre. The kits are pre dosed, so part packs have to be weighed, and the mix has to be placed inside a pot life of one hour at +23°C.

mapei/mapecrete-stain-protection.source: CONSUMPTION: 0.1-0.3 kg/m2 according to the level of porosity of the concrete. PACKAGING: 25 kg plastic drums.

tiers.label: By the level of porosity of the concrete
tiers.hint: Low end on polished or low porosity concrete, high end on rough or porous concrete

mapei/mapecrete-stain-protection.caveat: The sheet prints a single range and pins it to porosity alone, with no separate row per surface, so the whole span is shown rather than a chosen figure. Against the printed 25 kg drum that is 250 m2 at the low end and about 83 m2 at the high end. It is applied in one pass by airless spray or brush; the sheet prints no second coat.

mapei/planitop-raso-max.source: CONSUMPTION: Approximately 1.45 kg/m2 per mm of thickness. Application thickness: 2-10 mm.
mapei/planitop-raso-max.caveat: The 2 to 10 mm bounds are the sheet's own, printed both as the application thickness and on the bag. The 3 mm default is the calculator's, because the sheet names no recommended thickness within that range: set it to the job. The sheet also prints the mix as 100 kg of powder to 22-24 kg of water, which is the 5.5-6.0 litres it tells you to put in the bucket before a 25 kg bag, and a fresh mix density of 1700 kg/m3.

mapei/pulicol-2000.source: COVERAGE: Coverage depends on the amount and type of adhesive: as a general rule, coverage is 0.3 kg/m2.

tiers.label: General rule, one application
tiers.hint: The only rate the sheet prints

mapei/pulicol-2000.caveat: The sheet prints one rate and says coverage depends on the amount and type of adhesive being removed, so 0.3 kg/m2 is a general rule and not a guarantee. It also says that in certain circumstances a second application may be necessary, which is the second application on the control above and doubles the quantity.

mapei/epojet-lv.source: CONSUMPTION: Epojet LV Bonding concrete-steel: 1.1 kg/m2 per mm of thickness. Emirates edition, document 365-11-2024 (UAE).

pack.label: kit, component A 3.2 kg plus component B 0.8 kg

mapei/epojet-lv.caveat: The sheet prints neither a maximum nor a minimum thickness for the bonded plate rate, so the bounds on this control are ours, not the manufacturer's. The rate agrees with the other two figures the same sheet prints: sealing cracks by injection takes 1.1 kg per litre of cavity, and the density of the mixed resin is 1.1 kg per litre, since one square metre at one millimetre is one litre. The components are pre dosed 3.2 to 0.8, so a part kit has to be weighed on a precision scale, and the mix has to be injected inside a workability time of 35 minutes at +23°C or 15 minutes at +30°C.

mapei/eco-prim-pu-1k-turbo.source: CONSUMPTION: 80-100 g/m2 per coat. As a vapour barrier up to a maximum of 450 g/m2. The sheet quotes grammes per square metre, so the rate is stored in kilogrammes as 0.08 to 0.1 to match the 10 kg drum.

tiers.label: As printed, per coat
tiers.hint: 80 to 100 g/m2, by roller or brush

mapei/eco-prim-pu-1k-turbo.caveat: The sheet prints one rate and one ceiling. The rate is 80 to 100 g/m2 per coat, and used as a vapour barrier the total must not pass 450 g/m2, which is between four and five coats at that rate. One coat is the sheet's own recommendation on a porous substrate, a second goes on when the first takes light foot traffic after about 30 minutes, at least two are required where the residual moisture is above 5 per cent, and a third is checked for after that and broadcast with Quartz 0.8.

mapei/mapefibre-6mmpc-0.label: one 250 g sachet per bag of self levelling screed
mapei/mapefibre-6mmpc-0.source: CONSUMPTION: one 250 g sachet per bag of self levelling screed
mapei/mapefibre-6mmpc-0.caveat: The sheet quotes grams and this calculator answers in kilogrammes, so its 250 g sachet reads here as 0.25 kg. The bag counted is the bag of self levelling compound the fibres go into, not a bag of fibre. Sachets are supplied in boxes of 33.

mapei/mapefast-ha.label: 0.8 to 4.0 per cent by weight of cement
mapei/mapefast-ha.source: DOSAGE: normal dosage in concrete is between 0.8 and 4.0 % by weight of cement, which is 0.8 to 4.0 kg per 100 kg of cement
mapei/mapefast-ha.caveat: The sheet quotes a percentage of the cement weight and this calculator carries it in the same units, because 1 per cent of the cement weight is 1 kg per 100 kg. The sheet says higher dosages will only slightly improve the early strength, and that the admixture is best added at the same time as, or together with, the mixing water. Supplied in 200 litre drums, 1000 litre IBCs and in bulk on request, which the sheet quotes by volume rather than by the weight dosed here, so no pack count is offered.

mapei/mapefibre-ns12.label: 600 g per cubic metre of concrete
mapei/mapefibre-ns12.source: CONSUMPTION: the normal dosage of Mapefibre NS 12 is 600 g/m3, usually added to the concrete
mapei/mapefibre-ns12.caveat: 600 g is 0.6 kg, which is exactly one of the sheet's own paper bags, and the bags are supplied in boxes of 30. The sheet says higher dosages can be used for special applications such as shotcrete or fire resistance but prints no figure for them, so only the normal dosage is carried here. It also says the fibres offer no advantage structurally and are not an alternative to metal reinforcement. Added in the mixer together with the cement, aggregates, water and admixtures.

mapei/plastimul-dpc.source: CONSUMPTION: Approximately 2-4 m2 / liter depending on the surface conditions. The application section prints the same figure as a total: The total coverage of all coats should be 2-4 m2 / liter. The sheet quotes an area per litre, which is inverted here into litres per square metre.

tiers.label: Primer coat plus two neat coats, total of all coats
tiers.hint: 4 m2 per litre inverted is 0.25 litres per m2, 2 m2 per litre inverted is 0.5

mapei/plastimul-dpc.caveat: The printed 2 to 4 m2 per litre is the total for every coat, the diluted primer coat and both neat coats together, so there is no coats control and the figure must not be multiplied by a coat count. The sheet says the rate depends on the surface conditions and gives no separate figure for rough or porous substrates.

mapei/plastimul-dpm.source: CONSUMPTION: Approximately 3-5 m2/ liter per coat depending on the application area and the surface conditions. The sheet quotes an area per litre, which is inverted here into litres per square metre.

tiers.label: Neat, by roller, brush or spray, per coat
tiers.hint: 5 m2 per litre inverted is 0.2 litres per m2, 3 m2 per litre inverted is 0.3333

mapei/plastimul-dpm.caveat: Unlike Plastimul DPC, this sheet quotes its coverage per coat, so the coat count multiplies it. The sheet asks for two neat coats over a primer coat and says higher thickness may be applied with multiple coats, which is why three coats is offered. The primer coat is Plastimul DPM diluted with 10 to 20 % water on very porous or dry surfaces and the sheet gives it no rate of its own, so it is not counted here.

mapei/purtop-easy.source: CONSUMPTION: 2 kg/m2 corresponds to approx. 1.2 mm dry thickness. 2 divided by 1.2 is the 1.667 kg/m2 per mm used here.
mapei/purtop-easy.caveat: Thickness is the finished total thickness of the membrane, not the thickness of one coat: the sheet asks for at least two coats to a total higher than 1.2 mm, or a single 1.2 mm coat when the product is admixed with Purtop ADY, and both routes use the same material. The sheet prints a minimum of 1.2 mm and no maximum, so the 2 mm upper bound here is ours, not the manufacturer's. 1.2 mm is the default because it is the thickness every performance figure in the sheet was measured at. The sheet adds that the rate is for a seamless film on a flat surface and will be higher on uneven substrates, without saying by how much.

tiers.label: Roller, brush or trowel, two coats of approx. 0.4 mm
tiers.hint: The sheet quotes one figure for the finished two coat film, not a rate per coat

mapei/mapelastic-aquadefense-zero.caveat: The printed 1 kg/m2 is the total for the two coats the sheet requires, applied at approximately 0.4 mm each, so there is no single coat option and no coats control: one coat is not a permitted build up. Where Mapetex 50 is embedded as an anti fracture membrane the sheet says the final film is thicker and drying is slower, but it does not say by how much, so nothing is added here for it.

mapei/ultracare-grout-protector-spray.source: CONSUMPTION: Up to 30 m2 of porcelain tiles surface using one 750 ml flask of UltraCare Grout Protector (one coat), according to the surface finish of the material. 750 ml over 30 m2 is 25 ml/m2.

tiers.label: Polished porcelain tiles, one coat
tiers.hint: One 750 ml bottle covers up to 30 m2

mapei/ultracare-grout-protector-spray.caveat: Up to 30 m2 per bottle is the printed maximum yield, so 25 ml/m2 is the lightest case and a coarser or more absorbent finish takes more, which the sheet does not quantify. Treating the joints alone is a different sum again: the sheet puts one bottle at up to 800 linear metres of joint, heavily influenced by the joint size and absorption rate, and that is a length and not an area so it is not calculated here.

mapei/quartz.reason: Quoted by the resin, not by the sand. The range sheet prints its consumption as "dependant on type of use" and tells the reader to take the figure, and the choice of grade, from the data sheet of the epoxy, polyurethane or cementitious product the quartz goes into. Supplied in 25 kg bags.

mapei/prosfas.source: CONSUMPTION: Surfaces of screeds can be repaired using 0.5 to 0.7 kg/m2 of Prosfas but very porous surfaces may require four to six times as much.

tiers.label: Screed surface
tiers.hint: A cementitious screed with a crumbly or dusty surface, which is the case the sheet names

tiers.label: Very porous surface, four to six times as much
tiers.hint: The sheet's own multiplier of four to six applied to its 0.5 to 0.7 rate

mapei/prosfas.caveat: The sheet prints one rate and one multiplier rather than a table, and the second row here is that multiplier worked through: four times 0.5 and six times 0.7. The first row is preselected because the sheet names it as the rate for repairing screed surfaces and treats the porous case as the exception, not because it is the smaller number. Mapei also says to test a small area first and to apply several coats on very friable or damaged substrates, waiting for each coat to dry, and publishes no separate rate per coat.

mapei/primer-mf.source: CONSUMPTION: 0.2-0.4 kg/m2 per coat, depending on the evenness and absorption of the substrate (200 g/m2 per application layer). The sheet prints one range and no substrate table.

tiers.label: Per coat, as printed
tiers.hint: Depending on the evenness and absorption of the substrate, with 200 g/m2 quoted as the figure per application layer

pack.label: kit, 3 kg part A plus 1 kg part B

mapei/primer-mf.caveat: Two coats is the default because that is what the sheet asks for: apply in at least 2 coats, waiting about 3 hours between them and never more than 12 to 24 hours, the first by trowel and the second by roller, which is how the continuous film a moisture barrier needs is actually achieved. One coat is the sheet's own allowance for use as a consolidating agent only, so it is the lighter case and not the default. The printed rate is of the mixed product as supplied. The first coat may be thinned with Primer KL, at most one 1 litre bottle equal to 0.8 kg per 4 kg kit, which stretches penetration rather than coverage and is given no separate consumption figure. Also available in 1 kg kits.

mapei/primer-lt.source: CONSUMPTION: when applied between the layers of Ultratop Loft the consumption is approximately 0.1 kg/m2. On other substrates, the consumption is from 0.1 to 0.2 kg/m2 depending on the absorbency and the method of application. Both printed rows are here, in printed order.

tiers.label: Between the layers of Ultratop Loft
tiers.hint: Diluted 1:1 with water by weight, on horizontal and vertical surfaces

tiers.label: On other substrates
tiers.hint: Depending on the absorbency and the method of application: cementitious screeds, concrete, gypsum, anhydrite, wood, marine plywood, chipboard and Terrazzo style tiles

mapei/primer-lt.caveat: The other substrates row is the default because it is the row that covers priming a screed, concrete or gypsum before a skimming mortar, which is most of the work; the 0.1 kg/m2 row is the intermediate coat between two layers of Ultratop Loft and is the lighter case. The sheet sets the dilution by substrate, 1:1 between Ultratop Loft layers, 1:2 on cementitious or anhydrite and neat on wood, but does not say which dilution its consumption figures belong to, so the figure is treated as product as supplied, which is the safe side for ordering. One coat: the sheet publishes no second coat. Internal use only.

mapei/mapeband-easy-h130.source: PACKAGING: 30 m long by 130 mm wide rolls. 10 m long by 130 mm wide rolls. APPLICATION PROCEDURE: joints between different pieces of Mapeband Easy must overlap at least 5 cm and be bonded with the chosen waterproofing product.
mapei/mapeband-easy-h130.caveat: The sheet publishes no consumption rate because nothing is spread: Mapeband Easy H130 is a tape bedded into the chosen waterproofing product along a corner, an edge or a control joint, so it is measured by the metre of that detail. The figure is for the 30 m roll; a 10 m roll is also made. Only the 5 cm lap at the end of each roll is counted here. The 90 and 270 degree pre formed pieces and the templates for 200 x 200 mm and 400 x 400 mm through holes are counted off the drawing as pieces, and the waterproofing product it is bedded into is a separate product with its own rate.

mapei/eporip-a-b.source: Eporip data sheet, CONSUMPTION: construction joints with a rough substrate 0.5-0.7 kg/m2, construction joints with a very uneven substrate 1.0-2.0 kg/m2.

tiers.label: Construction joints with a rough substrate
Construction joints with a very uneven substrate

mapei/eporip-a-b.caveat: The sheet recommends neither row, so this opens on the very uneven substrate rate rather than the lighter one, which is the figure that will not leave a quote short. The same sheet prints two bases that are not areas: sealing cracks takes 1.35 kg per litre of cavity, and bonding precast concrete elements or steel to concrete takes 1.35 kg/m2 per mm of thickness.

mapei/eco-prim-pu-1k.source: EC Prim PU 1K data sheet, CONSUMPTION: 0.2-0.4 kg/m2 per coat.

tiers.label: Roller or brush
tiers.hint: one coat is usually enough on a porous substrate

mapei/eco-prim-pu-1k.caveat: A second coat is recommended on particularly porous or deteriorated substrates, waiting at least 3 hours and at most 24 hours between coats.

mapei/mapefix-ep.reason: CONSUMPTION: according to the volume of the hole to be filled. The sheet prints no rate per square metre and no table of hole sizes, because what is used is whatever the drilled hole holds around the bar. Hole diameter, embedment depth and design loads come from Mapei attachment tables 2 to 8, published separately on mapei.com, and the sheet asks for them to be set by a qualified design engineer. An anchor is a count of round holes rather than a chase of a given length, width and depth, so a volume calculator here would ask the wrong question. Once the engineer has fixed the hole schedule, the printed density of 1.50 kg per litre turns the empty volume around each bar into kilogrammes. Supplied in 585 ml bi-axial cartridges, twelve to a box with twelve static mixers with extension tube, and the first three shots of every cartridge are discarded.

mapei/mapelevel-easy-spacer-l-i.reason: The sheet quotes this in pieces, not in kilogrammes or litres, so there is no rate to multiply: its table gives the approximate number of caps and spacers for an area of 10 m2 against the two tile dimensions in centimetres. Linear laying runs from 1,980 pieces per 10 m2 for a 10 by 10 cm tile to 28 for a 200 by 200 cm tile, and cross joint laying from 980 to 26, with rows in between that do not fall in a straight line, so read the pair of dimensions off the table rather than interpolating. Mapei adds that the rates are approximate and depend on the layout and the flatness of the tiles.

mapei/ultracare-keranet.reason: The sheet prints only that consumption varies with the dilution, the degree and type of dirt and the surface to be treated, so there is no rate to calculate from. The product is diluted 1 part to 5 or 10 parts water by weight, or used undiluted to remove engobbio, and is supplied in 1, 5 and 20 litre tanks.

mapei/primer-sn-a-b.source: CONSUMPTION: 0.3-0.7 kg/m2 per coat depending on the characteristics of the substrate such as roughness, absorbency, temperature, etc.

tiers.label: As printed
tiers.hint: The spread is the substrate: roughness, absorbency and temperature

mapei/primer-sn-a-b.caveat: The rate is of the mixed product, batched 80 parts component A to 20 parts component B by weight, so it is ordered in kits and not in single drums. The 20 kg kit is 16 kg of A with 4 kg of B, and a 5 kg kit of 4 plus 1 kg is also published. The sheet prints one range and no substrate table, so the calculator offers the range rather than splitting it into rows the manufacturer never published. Adding Quartz 0.5, which the sheet allows at 20 and up to 50 percent by weight for a scratch coat, increases the volume laid and is not in this figure.

mapei/mapecryl-eco.source: CONSUMPTION: MAPEI trowel no. 1 approx. 300 to 350 g/m2, MAPEI trowel no. 2 approx. 400 to 450 g/m2, roller approx. 200 g/m2, TKB A1/A2 approx. 250 to 350 g/m2, TKB B1 approx. 350 to 400 g/m2, TKB B2 approx. 400 to 500 g/m2. The sheet prints these rates in grammes per square metre; they are shown here in kilogrammes per square metre.

tiers.label: Roller
tiers.hint: The sheet offers a long pile roller for thin wall coverings only

mapei/mapecryl-eco.caveat: Ready to use, so the rate is of the product as supplied. The sheet lists each trowel and notch class without pairing one to a covering, and the only method it singles out is the roller, for thin wall coverings; TKB B1 is the default as the notch class for standard sheet goods, so change the row if the covering calls for another notch. Also supplied in 25 kg and 5 kg buckets.

mapei/cleaner-l.source: CONSUMPTION: Varies according to the amount of contamination to be removed: 5-20 g/m2. The sheet prints the rate in grammes per square metre; it is shown here in kilogrammes per square metre.

tiers.label: As printed
tiers.hint: The spread is how much adhesive has to be lifted off the boards

pack.label: canister of 1 litre, in packs of 12

mapei/cleaner-l.caveat: The rate is per square metre of floor that has actually been stained, not per square metre of floor laid, and the sheet publishes no figure for a whole floor. The pack is quoted by weight because the sheet gives the 1 litre canister as 0.85 kg, so the figure and the pack stay in the same unit.

mapei/triblock-p.source: CONSUMPTION: 250-300 g/m2 per coat on non-absorbent surfaces; 400-500 g/m2 per coat on absorbent surfaces. The sheet quotes grammes, divided by a thousand here to give kilogrammes.

tiers.label: Non-absorbent surfaces, per coat
tiers.hint: Old ceramic, porcelain, marble and terrazzo floors, and very smooth compact concrete

tiers.label: Absorbent surfaces, per coat
tiers.hint: Cementitious substrates and concrete carrying residual humidity

coats.label: Coats, applied criss-cross 4 to 6 hours apart

mapei/triblock-p.caveat: The sheet asks for two criss-cross coats, which is the default here. A third coat is only for the case where Triblock P has been used to smooth over and the substrate is still very damp. The third printed consumption line, 1.5 kg/m2 per mm of thickness, is for the trowelled smoothing mortar made by gauging Triblock P 1 : 0.5 by weight with 0.25 Quartz or 0.5 Quartz sand, which is a different operation and is not what this calculator quotes. The kit is 5 kg of mixed product, so the pack count is kits and the three components can only be mixed whole, 12 : 38 : 50 by weight.

mapei/monolastic.source: CONSUMPTION: Approx. 1.1 kg/m2 per mm of thickness.
mapei/monolastic.caveat: Thickness is the finished thickness of the membrane, not the thickness of one layer. The sheet prints a minimum of 1 mm and a maximum of 2 mm per layer, asks for at least two layers at least 6 hours apart, and says the total must not exceed 4 mm. 2 mm is the default because that is the thickness the sheet calls complete waterproofing and the thickness every performance figure in the table was tested at.

mapei/mapestone-pfs-2-visco.reason: Mapei publishes no consumption rate for Mapestone PFS 2 Visco. The sheet says consumption depends on the shape and thickness of the stone and on the width and depth of the joints, and those are a paving layout rather than a rate per square metre. What the sheet does fix is the joint: it must be filled completely and must be at least 25 mm deep, poured the same day the stone is laid. One 25 kg bag takes 3 to 3.5 litres of water. Send us the paving layout, the block size and the joint width and we will work the quantity through with you.

mapei/mapetop-n-ar6-light.source: CONSUMPTION: Manual application: from 1.5 to 2.5 kg/m2 per layer. Mechanical application: from 3 to 5 kg/m2.

tiers.label: Manual application, per layer
tiers.hint: Applied in two layers, the second sprinkled at right angles to the first

tiers.label: Mechanical application, single even layer
tiers.hint: One pass of the spreader over the whole floor

mapei/mapetop-n-ar6-light.caveat: The two printed rows are not quoted the same way. The manual row is per layer and the sheet requires two layers at right angles to each other, so a hand spread floor takes the manual row twice over. The mechanical row is the whole floor in one pass, which is why it is the default: it is the figure for a finished floor. Choose the manual row to see the rate for one of the two layers and double it for the floor. Product is sprinkled onto fresh concrete before it starts to set, so the quantity has to be on site with the pour.

mapei/lignobond-chiaro.source: CONSUMPTION: 800-1000 g/m2 with a MAPEI trowel for wood according to the type of substrate. The sheet quotes grammes per square metre; the rate is shown here in kilogrammes.

tiers.label: MAPEI trowel for wood
tiers.hint: The sheet prints one rate for every size and type of parquet and says it varies with the type of substrate

pack.label: kit, component A plus component B

mapei/lignobond-chiaro.caveat: Two component, nine parts of A to one part of B by weight, and the figure is for the mixed adhesive. The sheet prints no trowel table, so there are no notch sizes to choose between. Also supplied in 5 kg kits.

mapei/mapelastic-zero.source: CONSUMPTION: Manual application: about 1.7 kg/m2 per mm thickness. Spray application with rendering machine: approximately 1.85 kg/m2 per mm of thickness on flat surface, approximately 2.2 kg/m2 per mm thickness on rough surface with irregularities.

tiers.label: Manual application, 1 mm per coat
tiers.hint: Straight trowel, the method the sheet sets out first

tiers.label: Spray with a rendering machine, flat surface, 1 mm per coat
tiers.hint: Rendering machine with a skimming lance

tiers.label: Spray with a rendering machine, rough surface with irregularities, 1 mm per coat
tiers.hint: The only row the sheet prints for an uneven substrate

pack.label: unit, component A 24 kg bag plus component B 8 kg jerrycan

mapei/mapelastic-zero.caveat: The printed build up is two coats to a final thickness of at least 2 mm, and the sheet forbids more than 2 mm in a single coat. The rates are per millimetre of thickness, so the default here is two coats of 1 mm. Spray on a rough surface costs about 29 per cent more material than hand application on this sheet, so the method matters more than the usual rounding.

mapei/latex-plus.source: CONSUMPTION table, Latex Plus column: mosaics and small-sized tiles 0.7-1 kg/m2, medium-sized tiles 1.3-1.7 kg/m2, large-sized tiles more than 2 kg/m2. The Keraquick S1 or Keraquick Maxi S1 column of the same table is quoted in each hint.

tiers.label: Mosaics and small-sized tiles
tiers.hint: With 2-3 kg/m2 of Keraquick S1 or Keraquick Maxi S1 powder

tiers.label: Medium-sized tiles
tiers.hint: With 4-5 kg/m2 of Keraquick S1 or Keraquick Maxi S1 powder

tiers.label: Large-sized tiles
tiers.hint: The sheet prints more than 2 kg/m2, with more than 6 kg/m2 of powder

mapei/latex-plus.caveat: Latex Plus replaces the mixing water, so this is the latex only and the Keraquick powder still has to be ordered: the sheet doses it at 8 to 8.5 kg for each 25 kg bag of grey or 7.5 to 8 kg for each 23 kg bag of white. The large-sized row is open ended, the sheet prints more than 2 kg/m2. Used instead with Nivorapid the sheet prints 0.3 to 0.5 kg/m2 per mm of thickness, and with Planipatch 0.32 to 0.47 kg/m2 per mm, which this area calculator does not cover.

mapei/planex-hr-maxi.source: CONSUMPTION: the consumption rate of Planex HR Maxi is 1.7 kg/m2 per mm of thickness.
mapei/planex-hr-maxi.caveat: Thickness per layer, from 3 to 40 mm, both bounds printed on the sheet. The 10 mm default is a realistic single pass inside that range and is the calculator's choice, not a Mapei recommendation. The figure is powder only: a 20 kg bag is mixed with 3.8 to 4.0 litres of water, or 3.0 litres where the mix has to hold a fall, and neither changes the quantity of powder. A second layer is applied as soon as the first sets to foot traffic, about 1 hour at +23 degrees, otherwise the first layer is primed again.

mapei/mapeflex-ps-ns.source: CONSUMPTION: litres per linear metre, 0.050 for a 10 x 5 mm joint, 0.200 for 20 x 10 mm, 0.800 for 40 x 20 mm and 1.250 for 50 x 25 mm.

pack.label: pack of A plus B (4 litres)

profiles.label: Butt or expansion joint, rectangular section

mapei/mapeflex-ps-ns.caveat: All 4 printed cells reproduce exactly: a litre per metre is 1000 ml of joint section, so 20 x 10 mm is 0.200 litres. The sheet allows joints from 5 to 50 mm wide, asks for a 2 to 1 width to depth ratio, and sets minimum depths of 5 mm on metals, glass and other non porous surfaces, 10 mm on all porous surfaces and 20 mm on trafficked joints and joints under hydrostatic pressure. This is the gun grade NS ME, supplied in 4 litre A plus B packs, against 5 litres for the pouring grade SL ME; density is 1.55 to 1.66 kg per litre. Porous joint faces need a coat of Mapeflex PSU PS ME primer, which is a separate 1 litre line.

mapei/quartz-1-2-me.reason: The sheet gives consumption as dependant on type of use. How much sand a job takes is fixed by the data sheet for the resin or cementitious product it is blended into, not by the area being covered.

mapei/aquaflex-roof-hr.source: CONSUMPTION: Waterproof membrane: at least 2 kg/m2. Protective finish on bituminous membranes: approx. 0.5 kg/m2 on smooth membranes; approx. 0.9 kg/m2 on mineral-filled membranes.

tiers.label: Waterproof membrane
tiers.hint: Two coats around 0.4 to 0.5 mm dry each, never less than 0.8 to 1 mm in total

tiers.label: Protective finish on smooth membranes
tiers.hint: Reflective finish only, over an existing smooth bitumen polymer membrane

tiers.label: Protective finish on mineral-filled membranes
tiers.hint: Reflective finish only, over an existing mineral filled bitumen polymer membrane

mapei/aquaflex-roof-hr.caveat: The 2 kg/m2 membrane figure is the total for the two coats the sheet specifies, not a rate per coat, and the sheet quotes it as a minimum. Rows are in the sheet's printed order, so the first row is the heaviest and is the membrane build up the product is sold as. The sheet adds that the rates are for a seamless film on a flat surface and could be higher on uneven or absorbent substrates.

mapei/nivoplan.source: CONSUMPTION: Consumption depends on the thickness of the layer but typically is 1.5 kg/m2 per millimetre of thickness (1 cm of thickness = 15 kg/m2).
mapei/nivoplan.caveat: The sheet prints 2 to 20 mm as the thickness possible for one coat and a maximum of 2 cm at a time, so both bounds are the manufacturer's. The default of 10 mm is the sheet's own worked example, 1 cm of thickness = 15 kg/m2. Nivoplan is not suitable for floors.
